100.name: Introduction to Animal Health Science
100.desc: An orientation to current issues and challenges related to animal health and disease in a global context. An interdisciplinary overview of the role and importance of animal health in modern society and its relationship to agriculture, food safety and human health. Causes of disease and the principles of maintaining healthy animals. The history and development of animal health professions and their roles. Not to be taken if credit received for AN SC 375.
100.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

101.name: Principles of Animal Agriculture
101.desc: Principles and practices of modern animal production and management. Brief introduction to the structure of the livestock, poultry, and game ranching industries. Principles of animal management, breeding and feeding. Current issues in animal agriculture. Students gain direct experience with animals in production/research environments. Not to be taken if credit received for AN SC 200.
101.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

120.name: Companion Animals and Society
120.desc: Diverse and evolving roles of companion animals in human society. Pets and the companion animal industry. Topics include: behavior, cognition and training; breeds and breeding; performance; nutrition, health and physiology.
120.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

202.name: Poultry Handling
202.desc: Biosecurity procedures and principles and practices of animal handling in poultry. Students will gain direct experience handling poultry in a production environment. Course runs for 5 days just prior to term.
202.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

203.name: Cattle Handling
203.desc: Biosecurity procedures and principles and practices of animal handling in cattle. Students will gain direct experience handling dairy cows in a production environment. Course runs for 5 days just prior to term.
203.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

204.name: Swine Handling
204.desc: Biosecurity procedures and principles and practices of animal handling in swine. Students will gain direct experience handling swine in a production environment. Course runs for 5 days just prior to term.
204.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

205.name: Animal Husbandry Internship
205.desc: Hands-on internship with food production animals. Students will develop skills in animal husbandry practices and record keeping. Pre- or co-requisite: ANSC 101 and consent of instructor.
205.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

260.name: Fundamentals of Animal Nutrition
260.raw: Prerequisite: 3 units in BIOL or 3 units in CHEM.
260.desc: Function, metabolism, homeostasis, requirements and sources of nutrients and energy for animals. Laboratory will involve principles of diet formulation.
260.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

310.name: Physiology of Domestic Animals
prereqs: BIOL 57 units including 6 units in university-level chemistry
310.raw: Prerequisites: BIOL 107 and 57 units including 6 units in university-level chemistry.
310.desc: Fundamental principles of regulation and maintenance of the internal environment. Includes a review of mechanisms providing for homeorhesis and well-being of domestic animals in response to changes in the external environment (e.g., light, temperature, social).
310.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

311.name: Metabolic Physiology of Domestic Animals
311.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 310.
311.desc: The physiological basis of the metabolic processes in domestic animals. Includes a review of the physiological mechanisms and neuroendocrine regulation of digestion, metabolism, growth and lactation.
311.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

312.name: Reproductive Physiology of Domestic Animals
312.desc: The physiological basis of reproduction, fertility and embryonic development in domestic animals in relation to animal productivity. The study of the physiological mechanisms regulating gonadal function, fertilization, implantation, pregnancy and parturition as well as the physiological basis for sound reproductive management.
312.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

320.name: Livestock Growth and Meat Production
320.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 101 or 200 or 3 units in BIOL.
320.desc: Concepts of growth and development applied to meat production from farm livestock. Form and function of bone, muscle and fat. Livestock and carcass appraisal.
320.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

325.name: Equine Science
325.desc: An in-depth study of equine anatomy, physiology, husbandry and diseases, both infectious and non-infectious. Equine nutrition, behaviour and the horse industry will also be examined. Not to be taken if credit received for AN SC 110. Prerequisite: 30 units or (BIOL 107 and BIOL 108)
325.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

375.name: Animal Health and Disease
prereqs: AN SC 3 units of AN SC 100
375.raw: Prerequisite: 3 units of AN SC 100, AN SC 101, or ANSC 200 or consent of instructor. AN SC 310 or PHYSL 210 or (ZOOL 241 and 242) are recommended.
375.desc: Principles of maintaining healthy animals, and an examination of current issues related to animal health and disease. Infectious and non-infectious diseases that affect both animal and human health and may impact international trade and export. Principles and mechanisms of immunity, disease surveillance, pathophysiology, treatment, prevention, management and economic impact of specific diseases and risks of bioterrorism.
375.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

376.name: Animal Welfare
376.raw: Prerequisite: (AN SC 101 or 200) or (3 units in biology and consent of instructor) and 60 units.
376.desc: An overview of animal welfare as it relates to both food and companion animals. Discussion of the scientific and ethical components that underlie our evaluation of the quality of life that animals experience.
376.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

377.name: Food Animal Behaviour
377.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 101 or 200 or consent of instructor and 60 units.
377.desc: Basic behaviour principles for food animal species including their application in livestock production systems. Fundamentals of experimental research and design in applied ethology.
377.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

378.name: Companion Animal Behaviour
378.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 100, PSYCH 104 and 60 units.
378.desc: Basic behaviour principles for companion animal species such as dogs, cats, and horses, including application of fundamental training and learning techniques to resolve common behaviour problems.
378.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

384.name: Principles of Animal Genetics
384.raw: Prerequisites: BIOL 207 and AN SC 101 or consent of instructor.
384.desc: An introduction to the basic principles of animal genetics and their practical application in selection strategies, breeding systems, and methods of improvement for domestic animals.
384.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

400.name: Individual Study
400.raw: Prerequisites: Third year standing or higher and consent of Department. Note: May be taken more than once if topic is different.
400.desc: Project or reading course supervised by a Faculty member, requiring preparation of a comprehensive report.
400.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

410.name: Regulation of Reproduction in Domestic Animals
410.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 312 or consent of Instructor.
410.desc: Study of basic physiological mechanisms involved in the control of reproduction in domesticated animals as a basis for developing practical approaches for the regulation of reproductive processes.
410.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

411.name: Veterinary Immunology
411.desc: Application of immunological principles to the understanding of animal health and disease with a focus on livestock and companion animals. Students will apply a broad understanding of host-pathogen interactions and the basic mechanisms of disease progression to assess the short and long-term impact of pathogenesis to the health of animals, their caretakers, and consumers. Lectures will be followed by active discussion of selected readings.
411.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

420.name: Meat Science
420.raw: Prerequisite: 3 units in BIOCH, AN SC 320, or consent of instructor.
420.desc: The conversion of muscle to meat in livestock and poultry: definitions and measurement of carcass and meat quality; influences of pre- and post-slaughter factors on carcass and meat quality. The lab will consist of a two day field trip during Reading Week.
420.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

461.name: Ruminant Digestion, Metabolism, and Nutrition
461.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 260 or 3 units in NUTR.
461.desc: Integration of theory and practical concepts in ruminant nutrition, digestion and metabolism through topics such as energy flow in ruminants, protein systems and net feed efficiency. Laboratories will involve formulation of rations for various physiological states of beef and dairy cattle, economical rations, feed mixes, protein systems (degradable and undegradable protein systems) and net feed efficiency formulations.
461.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

462.name: Monogastric Nutrition
462.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 260, 3 units in NUTR, or 3 units in NU FS 305. Corequisite: AN SC 311 or 6 units in PHYSL.
462.desc: Nutrient utilization and requirements, feed ingredients and applied feeding programs for poultry and swine. Feed formulation strategies and current topics in poultry and swine nutrition will be discussed in detail. Not to be taken if credit received for AN SC 463.
462.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

464.name: Companion Animal Nutrition
prereqs: AN SC 3 units from AN SC 260
464.raw: Prerequisite: 3 units from AN SC 260, NUTR 301, or NU FS 305.
464.desc: Aimed at fourth year undergraduate students with an interest in companion animal nutrition. The course will focus on nutrient utilization and requirements of dogs, cats, and horses. Other companion animal species (mammals, birds, reptiles, fish, amphibians, etc.) will also be covered. Current issues in pet food nutrition and manufacture will be discussed.
464.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

471.name: Applied Poultry Science
471.raw: Prerequisites: (AN SC 101 or 200), AN SC 260 and  AN SC 310.
471.desc: Study of avian anatomy, physiology, behavior, and health as it relates to modern poultry production. Current management practices to optimize production efficiency and animal well-being are examined.
471.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

472.name: Applied Dairy Production Science
472.raw: Prerequisite: (AN SC 101 or 200), AN SC 260 and 310, or consent of instructor.
472.desc: Examination of the structure of the dairy industry, evaluation of management practices to optimize production efficiency and animal well-being, and integration of nutritional, physiological, and biochemical processes involved in production of quality milk. Laboratories emphasize practical applications, field trips, and discussion.
472.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

473.name: Dairy Challenge
473.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 461, AN SC 472 and consent of instructor.
473.desc: A team-based capstone course to train students to participate in the North American Intercollegiate Dairy Challenge programs held in the US or equivalent local programs. Students will work in groups to gain integrative and experiential learning and develop skills related to comprehensive evaluation of dairy operations and consulting presentation.
473.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

474.name: Applied Beef Cattle Science
474.raw: Prerequisites: (AN SC 101 or 200), AN SC 260 and AN SC 310.
474.desc: Examination of current and potential future production and management practices to optimize production efficiency and animal well-being in the Canadian and international beef industry. Laboratories emphasize practical applications, field trips, and discussion.
474.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

476.name: Applied Swine Science
476.raw: Prerequisites: (AN SC 101 or 200), AN SC 260 and AN SC 310.
476.desc: Evaluation of swine breeding, feeding, housing management, and disease prevention practices that optimize production efficiency and animal well-being. Laboratories involve analysis of production practices with a view to optimizing efficiency.
476.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

485.name: Animal Genetics and Breeding
485.raw: Prerequisite: AN SC 384 or consent of instructor.
485.desc: Application of genetic/genomic principles and methods to the improvement of livestock and poultry.
485.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

488.name: Animal Nutrition and Health
488.desc: An advanced course aimed at fourth year undergraduate students with an interest in using animal nutrition to work in groups and solve animal health problems. The course will focus on problems that are associated with animal longevity, mortality, morbidity, and welfare and will translate research findings into nutrition recommendations.
488.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

496.name: Research on the Human Animal Bond
496.raw: Prerequisites: AN SC 378 or (90 units and consent of instructor).
496.desc: Exploration of research methods and measures; critical appraisal of research on the human-animal bond; application of research findings to the improvement of human and animal welfare. Students will conduct library and empirical research in the laboratory component.
496.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

499.name: Integrative Project in Animal Health or Animal Science
499.desc: A team-based capstone course exploring broad areas of animal health or animal science. Students will work in groups with mentors on a project involving experiential learning and skill development related to the field.
499.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

200.name: Human Morphology
200.desc: An introductory survey course in general human anatomy. The course covers the gross and microscopic anatomy of the tissues, organs and organ systems of the body, with emphasis on the relationships, interactions and functions of major structures.

305.name: Cross-Sectional Anatomy
305.raw: Prerequisite: ANAT 200 or permission of the Department.
305.desc: A study of human gross anatomy from a regional perspective, with a particular emphasis on cross-sectional structure and three-dimensional relationships. Students will apply their knowledge to correlate prosected human cadaveric specimens with  radiological images derived from a variety  of techniques. This course is intended to prepare students who are considering a career in applied radiological imaging and radiotherapy.

400.name: Human Embryonic Development
400.raw: Prerequisite: ANAT 200 or consent of Division. Note: Credit will be granted for only one of ANAT 300 or 400.
400.desc: A study of the development of the human embryo from conception to birth. The development of cells, tissues and organs of specific major structures will be covered including their relative development to other systems and structures.  An understanding of anomalous development and the ability to survive will be included based on a thorough understanding of normal development.

401.name: Human Neuroanatomy
401.raw: Prerequisite: ANAT 200 or consent of Division. Note: Credit will be granted for only one of ANAT 301 or 401.
401.desc: A study of the human nervous system including its development and function from an anatomical viewpoint. Both the central and peripheral nervous systems will be presented with some emphasis on abnormal development and its consequences. There will be an emphasis on clinical application where appropriate.

403.name: The Human Body
403.raw: Prerequisite: ANAT 200 or equivalent and consent of Division.
403.desc: A detailed, regional study of the gross anatomy of the human body using functional, clinical, and evolutionary perspectives. Will include lectures and laboratory sessions involving dissection of human cadavers.

490.name: Individual Study
490.raw: Prerequisite: consent of Division.
490.desc: Registration is contingent upon a student having made prior arrangements with a Faculty member in the Division. Credit may be obtained for this course more than once. This is primarily a supervised self-study in any of the anatomical disciplines.

491.name: Current Topics in Anatomy
491.desc: Discussion of topics relevant to the anatomical disciplines.  Credit may be obtained for this course more than once.

500.name: Human Development
500.raw: Prerequisite: ANAT 200 or consent of Division. Restricted to students registered in the Pathologist's Assistant program.
500.desc: A study of human development from conception to birth. The formation of tissues and organ systems will be covered, including their relations to other developing systems and structures. An understanding of anomalous development and the ability to survive will be included based on thorough understanding of normal developmental processes.

503.name: Human Anatomy
prereqs: ANAT 200 with a minimum grade of B+
503.raw: Prerequisite: ANAT 200 with a minimum grade of B+ or consent of Division. Restricted to students registered in the Pathologist's Assistant program.
503.desc: A detailed, regional examination of human structure incorporating functional, developmental, clinical and evolutionary perspectives. This course will used both didactic and practical instruction, including the dissection of human cadaveric tissue.

603.name: Medical Histology
603.desc: Advanced study of human histology with an emphasis on the relevance of histological examination to clinical medicine. Students will participate in discussions and complete a web-based interactive program.

606.name: Selected Topics in Advanced Human Anatomy
606.desc: An in-depth, supervised, self-directed study focussing on topics relevant to the anatomical disciplines. Credit may be obtained for this course more than once. Registration is contingent upon a student having made prior arrangements with a Faculty member in the Division.

607.name: Current Topics in Human Anatomy
607.desc: Discussion of topics relevant to the anatomical disciplines. Credit may be obtained for this course more than once.

497B.name: Research Project
497B.desc: Directed research carried out in the laboratory of an assigned member of the Division. Credit for this course may be obtained more than once. Successful completion requires a written report and oral presentation on the research project. Registration is contingent upon a student having made prior arrangements with a Faculty member in the Division.

497A.name: Research Project
497A.desc: Directed research carried out in the laboratory of an assigned member of the Division. Credit for this course may be obtained more than once. Successful completion requires a written report and oral presentation on the research project. Registration is contingent upon a student having made prior arrangements with a Faculty member in the Division.

600B.name: Medical Gross Anatomy
600B.desc: Advanced study of human gross anatomy. Will entail supervised, self-directed, hands-on dissection by the student for the examination of human structure and function. Particular emphasis will be placed on the clinical relevance of Human Anatomy and its importance to clinical medicine.

600A.name: Medical Gross Anatomy
600A.desc: Advanced study of human gross anatomy. Will entail supervised, self-directed, hands-on dissection by the student for the examination of human structure and function. Particular emphasis will be placed on the clinical relevance of Human Anatomy and its importance to clinical medicine.

140.name: Anatomie
140.desc: Introduction aux structures du corps humain. Doit être complété avant l'année 2 du BScInf (bilingue). Note(s): (1) La priorité sera accordée aux étudiants du BScInf (bilingue). (2) Ce cours n'est pas accessible aux étudiants ayant ou postulant des crédits pour NURS 140.

200.name: Morphologie Humaine
200.desc: Introduction à l'anatomie du corps humain. Le cours traite de l'anatomie macroscopique et microscopique des tissus, organes et des systèmes du corps humain, en mettant l'accent sur les relations, les interactions et les fonctions des structures majeures. Note : Ce cours n'est pas accessible aux étudiants ayant ou postulant des crédits pour ANATE 140, ANAT 200, ou NURS 140.

409.name: Histologie Humaine
409.desc: Ce cours d'introduction à l'histologie mettra l'accent sur la reconnaissance et l'identification de la structure et de l'organisation cellulaire associée à la physiologie normale des divers tissus et organes du corps humain. Ce cours comportera une part égale de cours théoriques et de laboratoires étant donné qu'il est essentiel d'acquérir et développer le sens de l'observation nécessaire à l'étude de l'histologie. Ce cours devrait permettre une compréhension de la relation étroite entre l'histologie, la physiologie et la pratique médicale. Préalables: BIOLE 201, PHYSE 210, ou PHYSL 210, ou PHYSL 212 et 214, ou ZOOL 241 et 242.

122.name: Texts and Contexts
122.raw: Prerequisite: English Language Arts 30-1 or ANGL 102 or ALS 125 or equivalent.
122.desc: This course explores a specific issue using a variety of genres and media. Not to be taken by students with 6 units in approved junior English/Anglais including ANGL 101, 111, 113.

123.name: Language, Literature and Culture
123.raw: Prerequisite: English Language Arts 30-1 or ANGL 102 or ALS 125 or equivalent.
123.desc: Studies in the literary and cultural uses of language. Not to be taken by students with 6 units in approved junior English/Anglais including ANGL 101, 111 or 113.

124.name: English Literature in Global Perspective
124.raw: Prerequisite: English Language Arts 30-1 or ANGL 102 or ALS 125 or equivalent.
124.desc: Studies in the literatures of the English-speaking world. Not to be taken by students with 6 units in approved junior English/Anglais including ANGL 101, 111 or 113.

126.name: Exploring Writing Studies
126.raw: Prerequisite: English Language Arts 30-1 or ANGL 102 or ALS 125 or equivalent. Note: Not to be taken by students with credits in WRS 101 or in ANGL 127.
126.desc: This workshop course focuses on both the theory and practice of the writing process to help students experience firsthand how university writers enter into rich ongoing conversations by engaging with the words and ideas of others.

127.name: Exploring Writing Studies for Nursing
127.raw: Prerequisite: English Language Arts 30-1 or ANGL 102 or ALS 125 or equivalent. Note: Not to be taken by students with credits in WRS 101 or in ANGL 126.
127.desc: This workshop course focuses on developing writing and communication skills by focusing on experiences in nursing, by nurturing foundational academic writing skills, and by guiding students through essential critical thinking skills.

199.name: English and Technical Communications
199.desc: This course aims to develop the student's ability to provide effective written and oral information. It will focus on instruction in fundamental writing skills, including building effective sentences and paragraphs, and on learning to communicate clearly across a range of genres and media used in academic and professional contexts, including correspondence and presentations. Students will be introduced to the principles of information gathering, analysis, and citation. Note(s): (1) Restricted to engineering students. (2) Not to be taken by students with credit in ENGL 199.

227.name: Communication and Writing
227.desc: A workshop course on communication and writing on contemporary issues. It focuses on genre knowledge, rhetorical knowledge, discourse community knowledge and writing process knowledge. The course will utilize write-to-learn and process-oriented writing strategies as ways to enhance students' ability to articulate course content and to engage in disciplinary writing, research and communication.

101.name: Introduction à l'anthropologie
101.desc: Une introduction à l'anthropologie par l'étude de concepts principaux et d'idées organisatrices tels que l'évolution humaine, l'apparition de la culture, l'organisation sociale, les théories de la culture, les systèmes symboliques, la dynamique de la culture. Note: Ce cours n'est pas accessible aux étudiants ayant ou postulant des crédits en ANTHE 202 ou 201.

207.name: Introduction à l'anthropologie sociale et culturelle
207.desc: Étude comparative de la société et de la culture humaine, en insistant sur la famille, la structure sociale, l'économie, les institutions politiques et la religion, les procédures de changement, et l'histoire de  l'anthropologie sociale et culturelle. Peut comprendre des sections Alternative Delivery; veuillez consulter la page Fees Payment Guide dans la section University Regulations de l'annuaire. Note(s): 3 crédits en ANTHE ou ANTHR sont fortement recommandés.

208.name: Introduction à l'anthropologie linguistique
208.desc: Étude anthropologique du langage et de la communication. Aperçu rapide des méthodes d'enquête sur le terrain et des méthodes analytiques et théorie de l'anthropologie linguistique. Note(s): 3 crédits en ANTHE ou ANTHR sont fortement recommandés.

220.name: Anthropologie sociale du vieillissement
220.desc: Portraits des formes de prise en charge des personnes âgées d'ici et d'ailleurs et analyse des impacts. Aperçus sur la vie post retraite. Note: Ce cours n'est pas accessible aux étudiants ayant ou postulant des crédits pour ANTHE 110 et ANTHE 120.

320.name: Anthropologie de la religion
320.desc: Introduction à l'étude comparative des religions et des phénomènes qui s'y rattachent; tels la magie, les tabous, le chamanisme et la sorcellerie. Des exemples ethnographiques sont utilisés pour appuyer une analyse des liens entre pensées et rites religieux et autres aspects de la vie sociale. Note(s): 3 crédits en ANTHE ou ANTHR ou autre science sociale sont fortement recommandés.

330.name: Variation biologique et environnement socioculturel
330.desc: Ce cours traitera des différences physiologiques et de leurs articulations sur les processus de vieillissement en fonction des environnements socioculturels. Des éléments de l'évolution et du comportement humain seront analysés. Préalable(s): 3 crédits en ANTHE ou autre cours de sciences sociales de niveau 200.

401.name: Médecines traditionnelles
401.desc: Principes et pratiques des médecines autochtone, chinoise, indienne (Ayurveda), africaine et autres. Analyse du paradigme du corps et de ses variances. Préalable(s): 3 crédits en ANTHE ou autre cours de sciences sociales de niveau 200 ou plus.

493.name: Anthropologie des enjeux médicaux
493.desc: D'une perspective multiculturelle et comparative : étude des croyances et des activités sociales associées à la santé et à la guérison. Les enjeux de langues et services de santé en contexte minoritaire sont analysés. Préalable(s) : 3 crédits en ANTHE ou autre cours de sciences sociales de niveau 200 ou plus. Note: Ce cours n'est pas accessible aux étudiants ayant ou postulant des crédits pour ANTHE 393.

101.name: Introductory Anthropology
101.desc: Introduction to past and present anthropological approaches through the study of human diversity.

103.name: Introductory Topics in Anthropology
103.desc: Consult the department for the specific topics offered. May be repeated if topics vary.

110.name: Gender, Age, and Culture
110.desc: An anthropological review and comparison of cultures in terms of social positions based on differences in sex and age.

140.name: Anthropology of Death
140.desc: Comparative survey of beliefs and customs surrounding death and the dead in past and present human cultures. Offered in alternate years.

150.name: Race and Racism
150.desc: The challenge of racism in modern societies and the response of anthropology, including the history of  how the 'race' concept has been used to explain human variation.

206.name: Introduction to Archaeology
206.desc: Introduction to the nature, purposes, theory and methods of anthropological archaeology. Emphasis on principles of reconstruction of past societies from archaeological evidence and the explanation of cultural evolution.

207.name: Introduction to Social and Cultural Anthropology
207.desc: Comparative study of human society and culture, particularly non-Western communities, with special attention to the family, social structure, economics and political institutions, and religion; processes of change.

208.name: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
208.desc: The anthropological study of language and communication. A brief survey of field and analytical methods and the theory of linguistic anthropology.

209.name: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
209.desc: Survey of theory and basic data in human evolution and human variation. Topics include primatology, osteology, hominoid paleontology, variation in modern populations.

219.name: World Prehistory
219.desc: A survey of the archaeological evidence for human cultural evolution.

230.name: Anthropology of Science, Technology, and Environment
230.desc: Science as a cultural practice, cultural effects and globalization of technology, changing views of nature, gender and science, traditional ecological knowledge, and the evolution of technology.

235.name: Anthropology of Disability
235.desc: Cultural variations in experiences and understandings of disability, as well as anthropological ways of analyzing and discussing disability. Offered in alternate years.

256.name: Alberta Archaeology
256.desc: Introduction to Alberta's past as reconstructed by archaeology.

286.name: Topics in Regional Anthropology
286.desc: Consult the Department and/or the schedule of classes for the specific topics offered. Variable content course which may be repeated if topic(s) vary.

287.name: Topics in Asian Anthropology
287.desc: Consult the Department and/or the schedule of classes for the specific topics offered. Variable content course which may be repeated if topic(s) vary.

301.name: Introduction to Ethnographic Methods
301.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 207 (or ANTHE 207) or ANTHR 208 (or ANTHE 208) or consent of Department. Not open to students with credit in ANTHR 401.
301.desc: Examination and practice of ethnographic research methods, including observation and interviewing, and forms of ethnographic writing.

302.name: History of Anthropological Theory
302.raw: Prerequisites: ANTHR 207 or 208 (or ANTHE 207 or 208) or consent of Department. Not open to students with credit in ANTHR 415.
302.desc: Major theoretical trends in social and cultural anthropology in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

303.name: History of Anthropological Archaeology
303.raw: Prerequisites: ANTHR 206 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years. Note: Not open to students with credit in ANTHR 481.
303.desc: A survey of the development of theory and method in anthropological archaeology.

304.name: History of Biological Anthropology
304.raw: Prerequisites: ANTHR 209 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years. Not open to students with credit in ANTHR 498.
304.desc: A survey of the development of theory and method in biological anthropology.

310.name: The Anthropology of Gender
310.raw: Prerequisites: ANTHR 110 or 207 (or ANTHE 207) or 209 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
310.desc: A comparative cross-cultural, and cross-species perspective on biological and social aspects of sex and gender differences.

311.name: Archaeology of Indigenous North America
311.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 206 or consent of Department.
311.desc: This course provides an archaeological perspective on the deep Indigenous histories of the lands currently known as North America and discusses how archaeology can respectfully engage with Indigenous peoples in ways that move toward decolonization.

312.name: Lower Palaeolithic Prehistory
312.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 206 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
312.desc: Development of prehistoric culture in Europe, Africa and Asia during the Lower Palaeolithic.

313.name: Middle and Upper Palaeolithic Prehistory
313.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 206 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
313.desc: Development of prehistoric culture in Europe, Africa, and Asia during the Middle and Upper Palaeolithic.

318.name: Political Anthropology
318.desc: Introduction to modern political anthropology with emphasis on origins of state structure, relations between non-state and state societies, and problems of pluralism and stratification. Offered in alternate years.

320.name: Anthropology of Religion
320.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 207 (or ANTHE 207) or consent of Department.
320.desc: Survey of anthropological approaches to religions and related phenomena including magic, taboo, shamanism and witchcraft. Emphasis on the connection between religious ideas and practices and other aspects of social life in a variety of cultures.

321.name: Religions of China in Practice
321.desc: Contemporary Chinese religious culture as practices in the family, community, voluntary associations, and the political sphere. Offered in alternate years.

322.name: Anthropological Perspectives on Discursive Practices
322.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 208 (or ANTHE 208) or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
322.desc: Cultural constructions of narrative and discourse; interethnic communication, including discourse in the courtroom, classroom, and work settings; code choice; and communication via electronic media.

324.name: Economic Anthropology
324.desc: Introduction to the literature and controversies within the field, emphasizing systems of exchange. Offered in alternate years.

325.name: Anthropology of Japan
325.raw: Prerequisite: Any 200-level Anthropology course or consent of Department.
325.desc: Exploration of anthropological writing on Japan as a case study in history of ideas and sociology of knowledge.

332.name: Anthropology of Science
332.desc: Contemporary views of the nature of science, including debates about science's universalism, objectives, and culture-bound epistemologies. Offered in alternate years.

333.name: Anthropology of Time and Space
333.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 207 or consent of Department.
333.desc: Study of classical debates on the social/cultural inflections of time and contemporary concerns with temporalities of industrial and post-industrial ages.

350.name: Kinship and Social Structure
350.desc: Anthropological approaches to kinship systems and other concepts of social organization, emphasizing non-western societies. Offered in alternate years.

372.name: Anthropology of Food
372.desc: Examination of the relationship between food and culture through historical and cross-cultural analysis of foodways. Offered in alternate years.

385.name: Topics in Social Cultural Anthropology
385.desc: Consult the Department for the specific topics offered and any recommended courses to be completed prior to registering.

386.name: Topics in Biological Anthropology or Archaeology
386.desc: Consult the Department for the specific topics offered and any recommended courses to be completed prior to registering.

390.name: Human Osteology
390.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 209 or consent of Department.
390.desc: Lecture and laboratory study of human skeletal biology, emphasizing the identification of bones and an understanding of human functional anatomy.

391.name: Hominid Evolution
391.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 209 or consent of Department.
391.desc: A survey of the fossil evidence for human evolution.

393.name: Health and Healing
393.desc: A cross-cultural study through time of the beliefs and social activities associated with health, illness and healing.

396.name: Archaeological Field Training
396.raw: Prerequisites: ANTHR 206 or equivalent, and consent of Department. Requires payment of additional student instructional support fees. Refer to the Tuition and Fees page in the University Regulations section of the Calendar.
396.desc: Instruction in all practical aspects of archaeological field techniques, including excavation, survey, recording, photography, and conservation. This course can be applied to the Canadian content requirement when held at a Canadian site.

397.name: Anthropological Field Training
397.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 207 or equivalent, and consent of Department. Requires payment of additional student instructional support fees. Refer to the Tuition and Fees page in the University Regulations section of the Calendar.
397.desc: Practical aspects of field training in socio-cultural anthropology.

407.name: Paleopathology
407.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 390 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
407.desc: A detailed survey of disease processes in antiquity as expressed in skeletal and preserved tissues.

411.name: Ethnographic Field Methods
411.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 207 (or ANTHE 207) or consent of Department.
411.desc: Study of methods used in ethnographic research, with a focus on addressing methodological challenges, developing a research project, and writing a proposal.

417.name: Anthropology of Modernity
417.desc: The course investigates recent works that theorize modernity (globalization, transnationalism, the impact of new technologies) from an ethnographic perspective. Offered in alternate years.

420.name: Anthropology and the Twentieth Century
420.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 207 (or ANTHE 207) or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
420.desc: The relationship between the development of anthropological theory across the twentieth century and the emergence of new social movement organized around anti-colonialism, anti-racism, feminism, ethnicity, the environment, gender, sexuality, disability, and identity.

423.name: Anthropological Approaches to Verbal Performance
423.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 207 or 208 or consent of Department.
423.desc: Attention to figurative language and rhetorics in everyday life as well as narrative forms, inlcuding myth, folklore and oral history, and to ritual language, inlcuding oratory and prayer.

424.name: Visual Anthropology
424.raw: Prerequisite: consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
424.desc: Introduction to visual media and visualization in the creation, reproduction and comprehension of culture over time, and the use of imagery in describing the anthropological subject.

425.name: Anthropology of Art
425.desc: Review of both classical and contemporary anthropological studies of artistic expression worldwide and questions concerning art as a cultural system, its function(s) and social position.

443.name: Juvenile Osteology
443.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 390, or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
443.desc: Study of the juvenile skeleton, treating development and identification of juvenile skeletal elements. Other topics include the theory and practice of determining juvenile age at death and the study of juvenile health and childrearing practices in past populations using skeletal remains.

464.name: Chemical Analysis of Bone
464.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 390, or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
464.desc: Survey of current research on the stable isotope and aDNA analysis of archaeological human and faunal remains.

468.name: Fundamentals of Archaeological Mapping
468.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 206 or consent of Department.
468.desc: Archaeological mapping and spatial analysis, including non-digital and digital forms. Students will learn the theoretical foundations of mapping as well as learn how to use mapping technology and software. Offered in alternate years.

469.name: Dental Anthropology
469.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 390 or consent of Department.
469.desc: Exploration of methodological and theoretical issues in dental anthropology through study of human teeth from archaeological contexts. Offered in alternate years.

471.name: Readings in Anthropology
471.desc: Individual research project conducted under the direction of a Department faculty member.

472.name: Independent Research
472.desc: Individual research project involving significant laboratory work conducted under the direction of a Department faculty member.

474.name: Northwest Coast Societies from an Anthropological Perspective
474.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 207 (or ANTHE 207) or 250 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
474.desc: A survey of the cultures of the Northwest Coast from Yakutat Bay to the Columbia River. Cultures will be examined from the perspectives of the ethnographic present, historical change, and current developments. Focal areas include social structure, kinship, economic systems, material culture, ethnoaesthetics, winter dance ceremonial complexes, and language.

476.name: Palaeodietary Reconstruction
476.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 206 or 209 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
476.desc: Survey of methods used to reconstruct past human diets, with an emphasis on those that involve the study of human remains.

478.name: Archaeology Collections Management
478.desc: Explorations of why and how archaeological collections are managed, introducing students to a range of practical aspects of the curation, collection, and stewardship of archaeological material.

480.name: Zooarchaeology
480.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 206 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
480.desc: Exploration of methodological and theoretical issues in zooarchaeology through the study of animal remains from archaeological contexts.

484.name: Topics in Archaeology and/or Biological Anthropology
484.desc: Consult the Department for the specific topics offered and any recommended courses to be completed prior to registering.

485.name: Topics in Social, Cultural and/or Linguistic Anthropology
485.desc: Consult the Department for the specific topics offered and any recommended courses to be completed prior to registering.

486.name: Seminar in Archaeology and/or Biological Anthropology
486.desc: Consult the Department for the specific topics offered and any recommended courses to be completed prior to registering.

487.name: Seminar in Social, Cultural and/or Linguistic Anthropology
487.desc: Consult the Department for the specific topics offered and any recommended courses to be completed prior to registering.

490.name: Human Osteoarchaeology
490.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 390 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
490.desc: The analysis and interpretation of data obtained from human skeletal and dental remains from archaeological sites.

491.name: Stone Tools
491.raw: Prerequisites: ANTHR 206 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
491.desc: A methodological and theoretical introduction to the analysis of stone tools.

494.name: Forensic Anthropology
494.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 390 or consent of Department.
494.desc: Human skeletal individualization and its application to human death investigation.

495.name: Archaeological Methods
495.raw: Prerequisites: ANTHR 206 or consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
495.desc: The application of archaeological theory and methods to field and laboratory problems.

497.name: Research Seminar 1
497.desc: Classroom seminar to develop skills required to carry out and present original research. Students will design and propose a research project, normally to be completed in Research Seminar 2.

498.name: Research Seminar 2
498.raw: Prerequisite: ANTHR 497.
498.desc: Completing a research paper or Honors Thesis under a faculty member's supervision.

500.name: MA Thesis Prospectus
500.desc: Preparation of a research proposal leading to the MA thesis. The prospectus will state the proposed research problem, and demonstrate the theoretical and methodological knowledge required to complete the research. Closed to web registration. Department consent required.

501.name: MA Colloquium
501.desc: Readings, presentations, and discussions of staff research, recent advances and current issues in the four fields of anthropology. Limited to new MA students

507.name: Advanced Paleopathology
507.raw: Prerequisite: consent of Department. Offered in alternate years.
507.desc: A detailed survey of disease processes in antiquity as expressed in skeletal and preserved tissues.

511.name: Ethnographic Field Methods
511.desc: Not open to students with credit in ANTHR 401 or 505. Offered in alternate years.

517.name: Anthropology of Modernity
517.desc: Investigates recent works that theorize modernity (globalization, transnationalism, the impact of new  technologies) from an ethnographic perspective. Offered in alternate years.

520.name: Anthropology and the Twentieth Century
520.desc: The relationship between the development of anthropological theory across the twentieth century and the emergence of new social movements organized around anti-colonialism, anti-racism, feminism, ethnicity, the environment, gender, sexuality, disability, and identity. Offered in alternate years.

524.name: Visual Anthropology
524.desc: Introduction to visual media and visualization in the creation, reproduction and comprehension of culture over time, and the use of imagery in describing the anthropological subject. Offered in alternate years.

543.name: Advanced Juvenile Osteology
543.desc: Study of the juvenile skeleton, treating development and identification of juvenile skeletal elements. Other topics include the theory and practice of determining juvenile age at death and the study of juvenile health and childrearing practices in past populations using skeletal remains. Offered in alternate years.

564.name: Advanced Chemical Analysis of Bone
564.desc: Survey of current research on the stable isotope and aDNA analysis of archaeological human and faunal remains. Offered in alternate years.

568.name: Advanced Fundamentals of Archaeological Mapping
568.desc: This course covers the basics of archaeological mapping and spatial analysis, including non-digital and digital forms. Students will learn the theoretical foundations of mapping as well as learn how to use mapping technology and software. Offered in alternate years.

569.name: Advanced Dental Anthropology
569.desc: Exploration of methodological and theoretical issues in dental anthropology through study of human teeth from archaeological contexts. Offered in alternate years.

571.name: Advanced Readings in Anthropology
571.desc: Individual research project conducted under the direction of a Department faculty member. Closed to web registration. Department consent required.

572.name: Independent Research
572.desc: Individual research project involving significant laboratory or field work conducted under the supervision of a Department faculty member. Closed to web registration. Department consent required.

573.name: Advanced Field Training
573.raw: Prerequisite: consent of Department. Requires payment of additional student instructional support fees. Refer to the Tuition and Fees page in the University Regulations section of the Calendar.

576.name: Advanced Palaeodietary Reconstruction
576.desc: Advanced survey of methods used to reconstruct past human diets, with an emphasis on those that involve the study of human remains. Offered in alternate years.

580.name: Advanced Zooarchaeology
580.desc: Exploration of methodological and theoretical issues in zooarchaeology through the study of animal remains from archaeological contexts. Offered in alternate years.

584.name: Advanced Topics in Archaeology and/or Biological Anthropology
584.desc: Consult the Department and/or the schedule of classes for the specific topics offered.

585.name: Advanced Topics in Social, Cultural and/or Linguistic Anthropology
585.desc: Consult the Department and/or the University timetable for the specific topics offered.

586.name: Advanced Seminar in Archaeology and/or Biological Anthropology
586.desc: Consult the Department and/or the schedule of classes for the specific topics offered.

587.name: Advanced Seminar in Social, Cultural and/or Linguistic Anthropology
587.desc: Consult the Department and/or the University timetable for the specific topics offered.

589.name: Advanced Seminar in Linguistic Anthropology
589.desc: Consult the Department and/or the University timetable for the specific topics offered.

598.name: Landscape and Culture
598.desc: Cultural experiences and representations of landscape.

600.name: PhD Thesis Prospectus
600.desc: Preparation of a research proposal leading to the PhD thesis. The prospectus states the proposed research problem, and demonstrates the theoretical and methodological knowledge required to complete the research. Closed to web registration. Department consent required.

601.name: PhD Colloquium
601.desc: Readings, presentations, and discussions of staff research, recent advances and current issues in the four fields of anthropology. Limited to new PhD students. Optional for students with credit in ANTHR 501

110A.name: Gender, Age, and Culture
110A.desc: An anthropological review and comparison of cultures in terms of social positions based on differences in sex and age.

110B.name: Gender, Age, and Culture
110B.desc: An anthropological review and comparison of cultures in terms of social positions based on differences in sex and age.

801.name: FSJ Cours d'apprentissage expérientiel I
801.desc: L'expérience professionnelle et l'apprentissage en milieu associatif ou communautaire offrent à l'étudiant une exposition à l'application pratique de sa spécialisation et à l'environnement de travail général. L'évaluation sera basée sur l'appréciation de la performance de l'employeur, le rapport de stage de l'étudiant, et la capacité de l'étudiant à apprendre des expériences acquises pendant le stage. Le stage devrait être d'une durée minimale de 130 heures (120 heures dans l'organisme d'accueil et 10 heures pour la rédaction du travail évalué). Préalable: l'approbation de la Faculté.

802.name: FSJ Cours d'apprentissage expérientiel II
802.desc: L'expérience professionnelle et l'apprentissage en milieu associatif ou communautaire offrent à l'étudiant une exposition à l'application pratique de sa spécialisation et à l'environnement de travail général. L'évaluation sera basée sur l'appréciation de la performance par l'employeur, le rapport de stage de l'étudiant, et la capacité de l'étudiant à apprendre des expériences acquises pendant le stage. Le stage devrait être d'une durée minimale de 260 heures (240 heures dans l'organisme d'accueil et 20 heures pour la rédaction du travail évalué). Préalable: l'approbation de la Faculté.

111.name: Beginners' Arabic I
111.desc: Introduction to pronunciation, reading, writing, and conversation for students who have not been exposed to conversational Arabic. Note: not to be taken by students with Arabic 35 or its equivalents in Canada and other countries. Not open to students with credit in ARAB 112, 113, 114.

112.name: Beginners' Arabic II
112.raw: Prerequisite: ARAB 111 or consent of Department. Note: not to be taken by students who have been exposed to conversational Arabic, or those with native or near native proficiency in reading and writing, or Arabic 35 or its equivalents in Canada and other countries. Not open to students with credit in ARAB 113, 114.

113.name: Beginners' Arabic I for Heritage Learners
113.desc: Introduction to pronunciation, reading, writing, and conversation for students who have been exposed to conversational Arabic, but have no formal training in spoken or written modern standard Arabic (MSA). Note: not to be taken by students with Arabic 35 or its equivalents in Canada and other countries. Not open to students with credit in ARAB 111, 112, 114.

114.name: Beginners' Arabic II for Heritage Learners
114.raw: Prerequisite: ARAB 113 or consent of Department. Note: not to be taken by students with native or near native proficiency, or Arabic 35 or its equivalents in Canada and other countries. Not open to students with credit in ARAB 112.

211.name: Intermediate Arabic I
211.raw: Prerequisite: ARAB 112 or 114 or consent of Department.
211.desc: Intended to expand comprehension and production skills in written and oral Arabic with a focus on intercultural competence.

212.name: Intermediate Arabic II
212.raw: Prerequisite: ARAB 211 or consent of Department.

399.name: Special Topics
399.desc: A variable content course, which may be repeated if topics vary. Taught in English.

173.name: The Plate, the Planet and Society
173.desc: A cornerstone course that provides an introduction to social perspectives on everything from what we eat for breakfast to how we protect endangered species and agricultural landscapes. Topics covered include current issues around food production and consumption and issues related to sustainability of our natural and social systems. Debates over new technologies (e.g., GMOs, nanotechnology), food, environment, and health can only be understood in the context of political, economic and personal decisions.
173.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

200.name: Economics of Agriculture and Food Issues
200.raw: Prerequisite: ECON 101 or consent of Department.
200.desc: Applications of microeconomic principles to problems and current issues in the agriculture and food sectors. Topics may include market structure, vertically linked markets, trade, the environment, and the role of government.
200.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

214.name: Applications of Quantitative Models to Food, Resources and the Environment
214.desc: An introduction to methods and tools that are used to solve quantitative problems related to agriculture, food, forestry, and the environment. Emphasis is on the use of these techniques for economic analysis. Students are introduced to the use of linear algebra, calculus and constrained optimization techniques. Classroom examples, laboratory assignments and computer tutorials are provided to give practice in applying quantitative tools to empirical problems.
214.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

250.name: Social and Economic Issues of Food Biotechnology
250.desc: This course will provide an introduction to the economics and business concepts in the biotechnology industry with an emphasis on food produced using genetic modification and other food technologies. The basic science behind GM foods will be discussed, but most of the material will focus on the social, economic, environmental, and legal issues surrounding GM foods. Key questions will be addressed using peer-reviewed literature and case studies, and the material will be presented from various disciplinary viewpoints.
250.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

313.name: Statistical Analysis
313.desc: Analysis of economic data relating to renewable resource sectors including agriculture, food, forestry, and the environment; collection of data, sampling methods, tests of hypotheses, index numbers, analysis of variance, regression, and correlation; time series analysis.
313.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

323.name: Introduction to Management for Agri-Food, Environmental, and Forestry Businesses
323.raw: Prerequisite: ECON 101.
323.desc: Principles and practical aspects of business management with application to agri-food, environmental, forestry, and related industries. The course introduces key management concepts used in planning, organizing, and operating small and medium-sized businesses. Topics include entrepreneurship, business planning, market strategy, financial evaluation, and the management of financial, physical, and human resources.
323.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

333.name: Economics of Production and Resource Management
333.desc: Application of economic concepts and introduction of management tools related to production decision-making for resource-based businesses. Integration of biophysical and environmental relationships with economic objectives in allocating resources. Introduction to quantitative tools used in applied production management decision-making.
333.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

365.name: Natural Resource Economics
365.desc: Economics of natural resources and the environment. Topics include resource scarcity, conservation, sustainability, externalities, pollution, and public policy for the management of renewable and non-renewable resources. Applications include water, fisheries, forestry, agriculture, land, energy, and climate change. Not to be taken if credit received for ECON 365.
365.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

375.name: World Food and Agriculture
375.desc: Economic issues in international agriculture including the world food problem, agricultural development; agricultural and food trade and policy and selected agricultural biotechnology issues. Selected international applications and issues are stressed. Not to be taken if credit received for INT D 303.
375.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

382.name: Food Systems, Distribution and Supply Chains
382.desc: Introduction to concepts in logistics, supply chain management and issues in food systems, distribution and farm-to-plate supply chains. Topics include product differentiation and competition in food retailing, local food innovation and food start-ups, food logistics and online marketing systems, Alberta food landscape and policy.
382.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

384.name: Food Market Analysis
384.desc: Applications of price and market theories to marketing problems and issues for food and agricultural products. Topics include: market structures and marketing functions; price analysis; futures markets; economics of food safety and quality; and international food marketing.
384.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

400.name: Special Topics
400.raw: Prerequisite: consent of the Department Chair.
400.desc: Individual study of a selected topic or problem supervised by a Faculty member, requiring preparation of written reports.
400.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

410.name: Advanced Methods and Applications in Applied Economics
410.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 313. Requires payment of additional student instructional support fees. Refer to the Tuition and Fees page in the University Regulations section of the Calendar.
410.desc: Empirical applications of methods used in resource, environmental, agri-food, and forest economics. Involves one or more case study projects that focus on the empirical examination of economic issues in renewable resource management.
410.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

423.name: Advanced Management Methods and Applications for Agri-Food, Fashion and Resource Businesses
423.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 313 or MARK 312. Requires payment of additional student instructional support fees. Refer to the Tuition and Fees page in the University Regulations section of the Calendar.
423.desc: Empirical applications of management research methods with applications to issues in agriculture, fashion, food, environmental and forestry industries. Emphasis is given to integrating economic and business management concepts in the development of professional business plans in areas such as agricultural, fashion, food, and resource industries. Capstone students assess the economic feasibility and analyze risks of business innovation and development strategies.
423.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

430.name: Economic Impact Assessment
430.desc: Examination of the theory and application of economic assessment methods with a focus on the evaluation of environmental, agricultural and natural resource projects, regulatory policy, and planning. Includes case studies of recent project and policy proposals to illustrate the methods used to evaluate economic benefits and costs of such proposals. Applications to estimating private economic benefits.
430.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

433.name: Financial Management in Resource Industries
433.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 200, AREC 365, ECON 281, or FIN 301.
433.desc: Recent theoretical and empirical developments in finance are applied to natural resource industries including agribusiness, farming, forestry and food. Emphasis on capital budgeting, financial risk, and associated topics for long run investment planning in smaller business enterprises.
433.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

460.name: Land Use Economics
460.raw: Prerequisite: ECON 101 and (AREC 313, ECON 399, or STAT 378).
460.desc: This course introduces concepts and methods employed in the economics of land use and land use change. Topics include: theoretical and empirical analysis of determinants and drivers of land use and land use change; environmental and socioeconomic consequences of land use change; the role of governments in managing land use decisions; and spatial analysis in land use research.
460.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

465.name: Advanced Natural Resource Economics
465.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 365. AREC 313 and ECON 281 recommended.
465.desc: Applied economic modeling of resource utilization and environmental issues with a focus in forestry and agriculture. Topics may include current Canadian and international issues in the area of environmental valuation, energy, climate change, biodiversity and conservation as related to Forestry and Agriculture.
465.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

471.name: Society and Well-Being
471.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 200, AREC 363, ECON 281, or ECON 365.
471.desc: Economic, political, historical, and legal perspectives on how and why governments promote well-being in areas such as food safety, nutritional policy, consumer protection, recreation, and the workplace. Topics include the historical development of wellness-related policies, how these decisions are made in society, and economic and moral justifications for such interventions.
471.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

473.name: Agri-food Policy and Trade
473.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 200, AREC 365, ECON 281, or ECON 365.
473.desc: Government policy affects our lives on a daily basis. This course focuses on economic principles and the analysis of agriculture and food policies in Canada and those affecting international markets and trade. The course enables students to develop a working knowledge of current Canadian agri-food and trade policy, while developing the analytical skills needed to critically examine agricultural markets, economic growth, and rent seeking within agricultural supply chains.
473.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

482.name: Cooperatives and Alternative Business Institutions
482.desc: The impact of agri-food and resource market structures on market conduct and performance; the impact of market structure on selection of cooperative versus investor owned firms including differences in firm objectives, performance and management incentives; topics may also include effects of firm type on community development and policy formation.
482.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

484.name: Strategic Management in Food and Resource Businesses
484.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 200, AREC 323, AREC 365, or ECON 281.
484.desc: Analysis of strategic management concepts and applications to agri-food and resource industries. The development of business and corporate strategies including competitive positioning; sustaining competitive advantage; vertical coordination and strategic alliances in value chains; corporate diversification and global business strategy.
484.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

485.name: Trade and Globalization in Food and Resources
485.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 200, AREC 365, ECON 365, or R SOC 355.
485.desc: Principles and policies affecting international trade in food, forestry and natural resources. Current issues in trade, including fair trade concerns, trade in capital and services, effects of food safety and quality standards, and environmental issues surrounding trade agreements and institutions.
485.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

487.name: Managing Market Risk in Resource Industries
487.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 200, AREC 365, ECON 281, or FIN 301.
487.desc: Study of the mechanics and economic functions of commodity futures and options derivative markets. Topics include the theory and practice of hedging, price formation and issues unique to commodities. Emphasis on concepts and analysis to evaluate derivative markets; use of derivatives to manage market risk in agribusiness, forestry and other resource businesses.
487.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

488.name: Introduction to Agricultural and Resource Game Theory
488.desc: Game theory analyzes situations in which payoffs to agents depend on the behavior of other agents. Basics of game theoretic analysis are introduced. Applications to the agri-food and resource industries are discussed.
488.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

500.name: Special Topics
500.desc: Individual study or special topics course in agricultural and resource economics under the supervision of a Faculty member.
500.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

502.name: Advanced Price Analysis
502.desc: Principles of consumer demand and producer supply analysis including theoretical and empirical approaches to the analysis of consumer and producer choice. Applications include food demand analysis (single equations and systems approaches), price expectations and producer supply decisions, market model simulation and policy evaluation, and economic welfare measurement. Pre or co-requisite: AREC 533.
502.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

513.name: Econometric Applications
513.raw: Prerequisite: Intermediate course in statistics or econometrics.
513.desc: Econometric theory, multiple linear regression analysis and interpretation, simultaneous equation estimation, qualitative choice models, time series analysis, applications of econometric techniques to resource and agricultural economic problems.
513.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

514.name: Quantitative Techniques
514.desc: Selected applications of econometrics, operations research, and mathematical programming to economic problems in resource, agriculture, forestry, and food sectors.
514.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

530.name: Economic Impact Assessment
530.raw: Prerequisite: AREC 200, AREC 365, or ECON 281, or consent of instructor.
530.desc: Examination of the theory and application of economic assessment methods with a focus on the evaluation of environmental, agricultural and natural resource projects, regulatory policy, and planning. Includes case studies of recent project and policy proposals to illustrate the methods used to evaluate economic benefits and costs of such proposals. Applications to estimating private economic benefits. Not to be taken if credit received for AREC 430.
530.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

533.name: Production Economics
533.raw: Prerequisite: consent of Instructor. AREC 313 recommended.
533.desc: Firm theory under perfect and imperfect competition, production principles applied to resource use, resource and product combination, cost structure, uncertainty and expectations. Notions of game theory and dynamic games, and the analysis of firm behaviour using industrial organization principles will be covered.
533.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

565.name: Economic Valuation of Ecosystem Services
prereqs: AREC 3 units in Introductory Econometrics course
565.raw: Prerequisite: 3 units in Introductory Econometrics course and consent of instructor; AREC 502 recommended. [Resource Economics and Environmental Sociology]
565.desc: Economic valuation of ecosystem goods and services. Topics include: Theoretical and empirical analysis of environmental valuation methods, advanced benefit cost analysis, welfare economics, valuation of ecosystem goods and services, valuation of health impacts from environmental quality change, and linkages to experimental and behavioural economics.
565.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

569.name: Advanced Topics in Natural Resource and Environmental Economics
569.raw: Prerequisite: ECON 481 or consent of Department.
569.desc: Theoretical analysis and modeling of renewable resource and environmental issues at local and global levels. Includes analysis of international environmental issues, the effect of economic growth on the environment, sustainable development, and local and global commons management.
569.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

575.name: Agriculture in Developing Countries
575.desc: Role of agriculture in the economic growth of developing countries; use of economic theory, simulations and contemporary econometric methods to understand the forces that shape the welfare of households and individuals in poor agrarian communities.
575.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

582.name: Industrial Organization in Food and Resource Industries
582.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor, ECON 481 recommended.
582.desc: Analysis of firm behavior and market structure in agri-food and resource sectors using industrial organization principles. Introduction to the internal organization of firms with applications to incentives, contracts, and corporate finance. Other topics involve ownership forms such as co-operatives; impacts of market structure on selection of firm structure; and the importance of firm objectives, performance and management incentives.
582.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

584.name: Marketing Economics
584.raw: Prerequisite: consent of Instructor. AREC 313 and 502 recommended.
584.desc: Microeconomic theory and analysis of markets for agricultural and food products. Topics will vary with the evolution of the literature but may include alternative market structures, market regulation, empirical price analysis, advertising, location theories, the role of information in markets, the role of uncertainty in markets, and organization structures.
584.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

600.name: Directed Studies
600.desc: Analysis of selected research problems and design of research projects in production economics, natural resource economics, or marketing economics.
600.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

613.desc: Analysis of economic data relating to renewable resource sectors including agriculture, food, forestry, and the environment; collection of data, sampling methods, tests of hypotheses, index numbers, analysis of variance, regression, and correlation; time series analysis. Not to be taken if credit received for AREC 313.
613.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

134.name: Art Fundamentals
134.desc: Studio-based exploration of both visual and conceptual Fine Art concerns in two- and three-dimensions. Note: ART 134 and DES 135 are required prerequisites for senior level ART or DES courses. Not open to students with credit in ART 131 or 132.

136.name: Art Fundamentals I
136.desc: Studio-based exploration of both visual and conceptual Fine Art concerns in two- and three-dimensions. Note: Restricted to BFA and BDes students.

137.name: Art Fundamentals II
137.raw: Prerequisite: ART 136. Note: Restricted to BFA and BDes students.
137.desc: Further study of studio-based exploration of both visual and conceptual Fine Art concerns in two- and three-dimensions.

240.name: Drawing I
240.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department. Not open to students with credit in ART 140
240.desc: Introduction to the principles and techniques of drawing.

310.name: Painting: Introductory Studies I
310.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department. Note: Normally ART 311 must be taken in the same academic year.
310.desc: Introduction to the principles, concepts, and techniques of painting. Projects based on observation with reference to both historical and contemporary examples. Acrylic medium.

311.name: Painting: Introductory Studies II
311.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department. Note: Normally ART 310 must be taken in the same academic year.
311.desc: Continued exploration of the principles, concepts and techniques of painting. Projects based on observation with reference to both historical and contemporary examples. Oil medium.

322.name: Printmaking: Introductory Studies (Silkscreen)
322.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department. Note: Normally ART 323 must be taken in the same academic year.
322.desc: Introduction to the principles and technical applications of printmaking through silkscreen techniques.

323.name: Printmaking: Introductory Studies (Intaglio/Relief)
323.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department. Note: Normally ART 322 must be taken in the same academic year.
323.desc: Continued exploration of the principles and technical applications of printmaking with the introduction of intaglio and relief techniques.

338.name: Special Projects in Studio Disciplines: Introductory
338.desc: Normally offered in Spring/Summer. Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135 or ART 136 and DES 138 or consent of the Department

340.name: Drawing II
340.raw: Prerequisite: ART 140 or ART 240, or consent of the Department.
340.desc: Development and application of techniques and concepts of drawing with emphasis on drawing from the life model.

350.name: Media Arts: Digital Media I
350.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department.
350.desc: This studio course explores concept-based modes of contemporary art production with an emphasis on digital media arts. Approaches may include: digital imaging, sound, video and animation.

351.name: Media Arts: Installation I
351.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135 or ART 136 and DES 138 or consent of the Department.
351.desc: This studio course explores concept-based modes of art production using expanded studio practices that include digital media, installation, performance, video, and other media-based practices.

352.name: Media Arts: Performance I
352.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department.
352.desc: Introductory studio course that explores concept-based modes of art production. Students use expanded studio practices that include performance and other media-based practices.

353.name: Media Arts: Lens-based Media I
353.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department.
353.desc: Introductory studio course that explores concept-based modes of art production. Students use expanded studio practices that include lens-based and analogue media such as film photography and video and other media-based practices.

354.name: Expanded Media: Special Projects I
354.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department.
354.desc: Introductory studio course that explores concept-based modes of art production. Students use expanded studio methods with a focus on critical fine art practices addressing special project themes such as the Anthropocene, Social Justice, Body & Technology.

355.name: Expanded Media: Variable Topics I
355.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department.
355.desc: Introductory studio class in variable topics such as kinetics, electronics, VR & AR.

360.name: Structural Sculpture I
360.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department.
360.desc: Introductory studies in sculpture with a focus on the constructed object. A range of approaches are introduced which may include woodworking, welding, assemblage, etc.

361.name: Formed Sculpture l
361.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department.
361.desc: Foundation studies in sculpture with a focus on the formed object. Approaches may include modelling in clay, mold making, casting and carving.

362.name: Soft Sculpture l
362.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department.
362.desc: Introductory studies in expanded sculptural practice. Approaches may include soft sculpture and fiber art.

363.name: Public and Social Sculpture I
363.raw: Prerequisites: ART 134 and DES 135, or ART 136 and DES 138, or consent of the Department. Pre- or Corequisite: ART 360.

101.name: Initiation à la recherche et à l'écriture universitaire
101.desc: Initiation à la rédaction scientifique dans les domaines des sciences humaines et sociales. Formation au respect des règles de déontologie de l'écriture scientifique (citation et constitution de la bibliographie) et en matière de rédaction d'un travail de recherche (structuration, constitution du plan, articulations). Note : Ce cours n'est pas accessible aux étudiants ayant ou postulant des crédits WRS 101.

399.desc: Étude d'un sujet au choix en Arts. Le contenu varie d'une année à l'autre selon les intérêts de l'étudiant et du professeur. Préalable : l'approbation du professeur. Note : Ce cours est destiné en particulier aux étudiants de la mineure individualisée.

490.name: Rédaction de mémoire II

499.name: Choix de sujet ou stage
