110.name: Introduction to Personal Health and Well-Being
110.desc: An individual-based analysis of physical fitness and personal health and wellness. Emphasis is on planning and managing one's own lifestyle for health and well-being within the context of the current healthcare system. The student-centred, applied learning approach of the course will promote relevance and use of health information to personal context. Open to all students.
110.faculty: Faculty of Kinesiology, Sport, and Recreation

120.name: Introduction to the Biological Aspects of Fitness to Health
120.desc: A biological analysis of the contributions of physical activity and exercise to fitness and long term health. Emphasis is on the introduction of training principles, health related components of physical fitness, exercise and physical activity guidelines, and the application of these concepts for determination of physical fitness, individual long term health outcomes, and preventable disease. Note: Credit will be granted for only one of HE ED 120 or HE ED 220.
120.faculty: Faculty of Kinesiology, Sport, and Recreation

221.name: Population Health
221.raw: Prerequisites: HE ED 110 or 120, KIN 101 and 103.
221.desc: The course focuses on the role of physical activity and other health behaviours in the primary prevention of chronic diseases across the lifespan. An epidemiological approach will be used to examine determinants, health behaviours, health outcomes, and interventions at a population-level in Canada and around the world.
221.faculty: Faculty of Kinesiology, Sport, and Recreation

320.name: Social Dimensions of Health and Health Promotion
320.desc: An examination of contemporary, social, political and economic factors as they affect health and well-being, with a particular focus on understanding the social determinants of health.
320.faculty: Faculty of Kinesiology, Sport, and Recreation

321.name: Psychological Dimensions of Health Promotion
321.desc: An individual-based analysis of health-related behavior and behavior change. Emphasis will be placed upon social psychological approaches to understanding and changing such health-related behaviors as physical activity involvement, dietary practices, smoking, alcohol and drug abuse within a social context.
321.faculty: Faculty of Kinesiology, Sport, and Recreation

421.name: Psychological and Behavioural Aspects of Chronic Disease Management
421.raw: Prerequisites: HE ED 221 and 321.
421.desc: An in-depth examination of the role of physical activity and other health behaviours in the secondary and tertiary prevention of chronic diseases. Relevant behaviour change theories and corresponding research will be used to examine health behaviour change interventions and other programs and initiatives used in the management of chronic disease.
421.faculty: Faculty of Kinesiology, Sport, and Recreation

210.name: Introduction to Biblical Hebrew I
210.desc: Fundamentals of Biblical Hebrew for reading and translation purposes. Not open to students with previous knowledge of Biblical Hebrew or credit in HEBR 201.

211.name: Introduction to Biblical Hebrew II
211.raw: Prerequisite: HEBR 210 or consent of Instructor. Note: Not open to students with knowledge of Biblical Hebrew that exceeds one semester of university study.
211.desc: A continuation of HEBR 210.

100.name: Introduction to Principles and Practice in Human Ecology
100.desc: An introductory course that provides a foundation in the body of knowledge that constitutes the field of human ecology (i.e., its history and philosophy; theories for studying everyday life). The scope of the field is explored and skills that foster effective professional practice by human ecologists are discussed.
100.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

170.name: Introduction to Textiles
170.desc: An introductory exploration of the origin, creation and use of textiles in our world. Chemical and physical properties of fibres and fabrics are introduced and an understanding of how these properties influence various clothing and textile end uses is developed.
170.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

201.name: Introduction to Material Culture
201.desc: The study of a range of objects and environments (from clothing to buildings) within selected time periods, and the study of particular perspectives through which such items can be interpreted. Students explore and learn about the connections between personal, social, temporal, and cultural contexts and the objects and environments that contribute to these contexts.
201.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

210.name: Intimate Relationships
210.desc: A consideration of the sociological, psychological, and personal factors affecting the development, maintenance and dissolution of intimate relationships today.
210.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

211.name: Human Sexuality
211.desc: An inquiry into the nature of sexual behavior, its personal and cultural sources, and the personal, familial and societal implications.
211.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

214.name: Seniors and Their Environments
214.desc: An introduction to the environments in which older people live. The course uses an ecological framework to study the symbolic, physical, interpersonal, community, and political environments of older adults in Canada and other world regions.
214.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

241.name: Fashion Industries
241.desc: An introduction to the soft goods industry including an overview of the apparel sector, apparel production, channels of distribution, fashion oriented products, global competitive influences, and career opportunities.
241.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

250.name: Design Studies and Practices
250.desc: Explores the production of designed things as material culture from a human ecological perspective. Theories and practices of object production focus on design processes including visualization, communication, inspiration/influence, and interface in the context of two-and three-dimensional design. Students learn theories during lectures and apply these in hands-on design projects in the studio.
250.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

254.name: Apparel Design and Construction Fundamentals
254.raw: Prerequisites: One of HECOL 250, 170, or DES 135 or DES 138/139.
254.desc: In this studio course students develop fundamental awareness and skills for the textiles and clothing field including machine operation, design and construction terminology, pattern manipulation and fit, and quality construction techniques. Students construct samples and garments with a focus on professional standards in problem solving and production.
254.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

268.name: Survey of Historic Dress in the Western World
268.desc: Introduction to the historical development of dress in the Western World with contemporary applications in design, merchandising, arts performance, education and museums. Resources include the Anne Lambert Clothing and Textiles Collection.
268.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

270.name: Applications of Textile Science
270.desc: Advancement of textile concepts introduced in HECOL 170 with an emphasis on textile finishing, colouration, care and maintenance. Techniques for fibre identification and yarn and fabric structural analysis are covered.
270.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

300.name: Policy Development and Evaluation
300.desc: Processes of policy development, implementation and analysis; Canadian policy environments, institutional frameworks and instruments; application to professional practice and to current social and economic issues.
300.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

301.name: Program Planning and Evaluation
301.raw: Prerequisite: successful completion of 60 units.
301.desc: Theories and processes of program planning, implementation, and evaluation from a human ecological perspective.
301.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

313.name: Family Dynamics
313.desc: An introduction to family dynamics from the perspective of family theory. Changes in family dynamics across the life course will be examined using theoretical concepts, research, and practical application of concepts.
313.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

315.name: Interviewing and Counseling
315.desc: An introduction to interviewing and counseling strategies for working with individuals using a strengths-based, human ecological approach.
315.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

321.name: Introduction to Family Finance
prereqs: it is recommended that students have completed both ECON 101
321.raw: Prerequisite: ECON 101; it is recommended that students have completed both ECON 101 and 102.
321.desc: An introduction to the principles of money management for individuals, households, and families. Students learn basic financial literacy skills and tools required to make key financial decisions by identifying financial goals, assessing current resources, developing and implementing a financial plan and evaluating financial progress. It is also expected that students will be able to apply these tools in their professional work to enhance clients' financial literacy and their ability to resolve financial management challenges.
321.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

322.name: Family Economic Issues
prereqs: it is recommended that students have completed both ECON 101
322.raw: Prerequisites: ECON 101; it is recommended that students have completed both ECON 101 and 102.
322.desc: An examination of current issues affecting the economic well-being of Canadian families and of government policies which address those issues. Issues explored include work and family; the economics of childbearing, education, delayed life transitions, and aging; intrafamily allocation of resources; and money and family relationships.
322.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

333.name: Cross-Cultural Textiles
333.desc: An introduction to the historical and technological development of cross-cultural textiles and survey of common textile-making techniques, designs, and embellishments. Ethnographic textiles are analyzed in the context of socio-cultural, political, economic, environmental, and aesthetical meanings. The course combines lectures, class discussions, videos, and examination of artifacts from the Clothing and Textiles Collection.
333.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

354.name: Apparel Design and Product Development I
354.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 254. Normally offered in alternate years.
354.desc: Principles of design and merchandising applied to apparel design and portfolio development. A creative problem-solving approach to production of a line of clothing.
354.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

360.name: Dress and Culture
360.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 268. Normally offered in alternate years.
360.desc: The complex phenomenon of bodily adornment is explored in relationship to values, attitudes, activities, beliefs, and forms of knowledge. Clothing is considered in terms of how it is expressive of various aspects of culture. Students develop analytical skills to help them understand the role played by clothing in different times, places, and contexts.
360.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

368.name: Fashion History: Interpretations & Exhibition
368.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 268. Normally offered in alternate years.
368.desc: Advanced study of Western dress from the 18th century to the present. Lectures and labs introduce students to artifactual research and the handling, storage, examination, documentation and exhibition of artifacts. Sources explored include artwork, fashion plates, texts, caricatures, photography, patterns, reproduction garments and historical clothing from the Anne Lambert Clothing and Textiles Collection. Students co-curate an exhibition as part of the course.
368.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

370.name: Quality Assurance for Textiles and Apparel
370.desc: Exploration of quality assurance of textiles and apparel through materials testing. Performance of textiles relative to product standards and specifications.
370.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

401.name: Interdisciplinary Ways of Knowing
401.raw: Prerequisite: Completion of 60 units.
401.desc: This course explores the key ideas, tenets, and turning points of various epistemologies in approaches to research in Western societies. It explores the nature and scope of interdisciplinary knowledge practices needed to examine complex problems.
401.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

408.name: Intentional Professional Practice
408.desc: Preparation for human ecology practicum placement. Effective workplace relationships and issues involved in professional practice are explored within the context of being a practicum student. Reflective practice and career development are key concepts of the course.
408.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

409.name: Practicum in Human Ecology
409.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 408. Requires payment of additional student instructional support fees. Refer to the Tuition and Fees page in the University Regulations section of the Calendar.
409.desc: Supervised field experience. Students are placed in professional settings appropriate to their academic background and career goals. Participation in a weekly online seminar is required.
409.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

410.name: Parent-Child Relationships
410.raw: Prerequisite: PSYCH 223.
410.desc: An exploration of parent-child relationships, with a concentration from infancy through adolescence. An examination of theoretical and research perspectives of parent-child relationships and the practical application of those perspectives. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 310.
410.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

412.name: Family Challenges
412.desc: An in-depth exploration of several family challenges (e.g. addiction, homelessness, and childhood and adult abuse). An introduction to specific prevention and intervention approaches related to family challenges.
412.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

413.name: Working With Families
413.desc: Assessment and counseling strategies for working with families using a strengths-based, family-centred approach.
413.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

415.name: Families and Aging
415.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 214 or HECOL 313.
415.desc: Current issues in mid- and later-life families including relationships between aging parents and adult children, grandparent relationships, family caregiving.
415.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

440.name: Family Policy Issues
440.raw: Prerequisite: 60 units or consent of instructor.
440.desc: Analysis of current policy issues faced by Canadian families and the examination of policies and programs affecting family well-being and relationships.
440.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

441.name: Conditions & Consequences of the Fashion Industry
441.raw: Prerequisite: 60 units and HECOL 241 or consent of instructor.
441.desc: This seminar examines the conditions and consequences of the global fashion industry, exploring how capitalism, globalization, labour standards, and international trade policies shape fashion as a social, economic, and political system. This course will analyze the fashion industry across diverse geographic and cultural contexts.
441.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

443.name: Family Law
443.desc: Family law regulates intimate and domestic relationships. Examines from a user's perspective, how statutory and common law affects family relationship issues such as marriage and divorce, child custody and child welfare, adoption, and new reproductive technologies. Normally offered in alternate years.
443.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

454.name: Apparel Design and Product Development II
454.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 254. Normally offered in alternate years.
454.desc: Advanced problems in apparel design and product development. Draping and fabric manipulation techniques are explored. The focus is traditional specialty fabric techniques and experimental production methods.
454.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

464.name: Fashion and Material Culture: Politics, Economies, Societies, c. 1600-1900
464.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor. Normally offered in alternate years.
464.desc: Examines the evolution and practice of fashion as a social, economic, political and cultural phenomenon from a cross-cultural perspective.
464.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

465.name: Research Methods for Material Culture and Design Studies
465.desc: Explores how to do research into the relationships between people and objects (from clothing to buildings). Students will learn how to conduct primary research through a range of methods, approaches, and theories associated with material culture and design studies.
465.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

469.name: Applications of Critical Design Thinking
469.desc: Explores how critical design thinking tools and methods are used within human ecological and systems approaches towards design, business, engineering and material culture issues. Includes research and practice topics such as human-centred, reflexive, and sustainable practices towards the innovation of products, exhibitions, spaces and services.
469.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

470.name: Advanced Materials for Protective Clothing
470.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 370 or consent of instructor.
470.desc: Students explore advanced materials for protective clothing. Resistance of textiles to mechanical, thermal, chemical, biological, and electrical hazards as well as questions of durability and comfort are discussed with an emphasis on current research. The course describes phenomena and mechanisms involved, presents appropriate materials and structures, and depicts the relevant test methods.
470.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

472.name: Environmental Sustainability in Textiles
472.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 170 and 60 units. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 372.
472.desc: Examination of the clothing and textiles industry and the environmental impact of textile production and consumption. Topics may include but are not limited to, circular economy, life-cycle thinking, environmental labelling, sustainable fibres, sustainable fabric and finishing technologies, consumption patterns and post-consumer use.
472.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

473.name: Clothing and Materials for Sport and Safety
473.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 370. Normally offered in alternate years.
473.desc: A human ecological exploration of the selection, use and performance of clothing and materials used for workplace safety protection and sporting/recreational activities.
473.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

474.name: Introduction to Nanotechnologies and Smart Textiles
474.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 170 and 60 units; or consent of instructor.
474.desc: Students explore opportunities offered by nanotechnologies and smart materials/structures as they relate to textile products. Mechanisms involved, materials used, fabrication processes, properties/performance obtained, and some examples of commercial applications are presented. Challenges encountered with these new technologies are also discussed.
474.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

476.name: Textile Analysis and Care
476.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 270. Normally offered in alternate years.
476.desc: Deterioration and preservation of modern and historical textiles are investigated. Macro and microscopic evidence are combined with theories of fibre degradation and textile soiling to identify the causes of wear, discoloration and failure during the normal use, care and storage of textiles. Theory related to the cleaning of textiles will include detergency, bleaching, dry-cleaning and specialized procedures for historical textiles.
476.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

490.name: Independent Investigation in Human Ecology
490.raw: Prerequisite: successful completion of 75 units, application to Department, and consent of Instructor.
490.desc: Independent project or study of a topic in human ecology planned by the student with an instructor. Open to human ecology students only.
490.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

492.name: Selected Topics in Family Ecology
492.raw: Prerequisite: successful completion of 60 units or consent of Instructor.
492.desc: Normally offered in Spring or Summer. Can be taken for credit more than once if the topics are different.
492.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

493.name: Selected Topics in Textiles and Clothing
493.raw: Prerequisite: successful completion of 60 units or consent of Instructor. Requires payment of additional student instructional support fees.  Refer to the Tuition and Fees page in the University Regulations section of the Calendar.
493.desc: Normally offered in Spring or Summer. Can be taken for credit more than once if the topics are different.
493.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

501.name: Independent Project in Human Ecology
501.desc: Independent study of a topic in human ecology planned by the student in consultation with the Instructor. Independent studies may be taken more than once for credit.
501.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

508.name: Graduate Intentional Professional Practice
508.raw: Prerequisite: consent of the instructor. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 408.
508.desc: Preparation for human ecology practicum placement. Effective workplace relationships and issues involved in professional practice are explored within the context of being a practicum student. Reflective practice and career development are key concepts of the course.
508.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

522.name: Introduction to Structural Equation Modeling
522.raw: Prerequisites: Statistics coursework covering regression analysis. Normally offered in alternate years.
522.desc: Provides an introduction to the theory and practice of structural equation modeling with social science data. Practical application in Mplus is emphasized by computing and interpreting statistical models within this framework, including path analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling.
522.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

532.name: Family Health and Wellness; Theoretical and  Measurement Issues for Research and Practice
532.desc: Critical examination of the conceptualization and measurement of family health and the interrelationships between the health of families and their members. Applications to research and practice in a variety of disciplines including family ecology, nursing, health promotion, occupational therapy, education, and psychology. Not to be taken if credit received in NURS 532.
532.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

550.name: Selected Topics in Human Ecology
550.desc: Topics of current interest. May be taken for credit more than once.
550.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

565.name: Material Culture and Design Studies: Methods of Qualitative Analysis
565.desc: Explores specific qualitative research approaches, theories, and methods that relate to the fields of material culture and design studies. Students collect, examine, and interpret data concerning people's relationships with items of material culture (including design). Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 465.
565.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

569.name: Applications of Critical Design Thinking
569.desc: Explores how critical design thinking tools and methods are used within human ecological and systems approaches towards design, business, engineering and material culture issues. Includes research and practice topics such as human-centred, reflexive, and sustainable practices towards the innovation of products, exhibitions, spaces, and services. Not to be taken if credit is received in HECOL 469.
569.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

570.name: Advanced Materials for Protective Clothing
570.desc: Students explore advanced materials for protective clothing. Resistance of textiles to mechanical, thermal, chemical, biological, and electrical hazards as well as questions of durability and comfort are discussed with an emphasis on current research. The course describes phenomena and mechanisms involved, presents appropriate materials and structures, and depicts the relevant test methods. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 470.
570.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

571.name: Review of Literature in Clothing, Textiles and Material Culture Studies
571.desc: Review of scholarly literature related to clothing and textiles sciences and/or material culture research. A literature review is a required part of this course. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 680.
571.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

572.name: Environmental Sustainability in Textiles
572.raw: Prerequisite: Consent of the instructor. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 372 or 472.
572.desc: Examination of the clothing and textiles industry and the environmental impact of textile production and consumption.
572.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

573.name: Clothing and Materials for Sport and Safety
573.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor. Normally offered in alternate years. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 473.
573.desc: A human ecological exploration of the selection, use and performance of clothing and materials used for workplace safety protection and sporting/recreational activities.
573.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

574.name: Introduction to Nanotechnologies and Smart Textiles
574.raw: Prerequisite: consent of the instructor. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 474.
574.desc: Students explore opportunities offered by nanotechnologies and smart materials/structures as they relate to textile products. Mechanisms involved, materials used, fabrication processes, properties/performance obtained, and some examples of commercial applications are presented. Challenges encountered with these new technologies are also discussed.
574.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

575.name: Fundamentals of Human Comfort in Protective Clothing
575.desc: Examination of heat and mass transfer between clothing and the human body in relation to comfort and protection.
575.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

576.name: Textile Analysis and Care
576.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor. Normally offered in alternate years. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 476.
576.desc: Deterioration and preservation of modern and historical textiles are investigated. Macro and microscopic evidence are combined with theories of fibre degradation and textile soiling to identify the causes of wear, discoloration and failure during the normal use, care and storage of textiles. Theory related to the cleaning of textiles will include detergency, bleaching, dry-cleaning and specialized procedures for historical textiles.
576.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

579.name: Research Methods in Textile and Apparel Science
579.desc: An examination of qualitative and quantitative research methods relevant to clothing and textiles scholarship.
579.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

601.name: Ways of Knowing in Human Ecology
601.desc: Enquiry into the nature, scope and object of human ecology knowledge; the distinct contributions of various modes of inquiry; and the relationship between ways of knowing and selected issues related to the acquisition of knowledge, such as ethics and research methods.
601.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

604.name: Fundamentals of Aging
604.desc: A critical analysis of the issues and environments that influence the lives of older Canadians. Focus  is on theories and knowledge about age-related normative and non-normative changes and their interaction with the physical, social, community and policy environments of older adults.
604.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

610.name: Review of Issues and Trends in Family Ecology and Practice
610.desc: Content and philosophy of the study of the family from a human ecological perspective.
610.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

611.name: Theory in Family Ecology
611.raw: Pre or corequisite: HECOL 610 or consent of Instructor.
611.desc: Consideration of family theory as it relates to research and practice.
611.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

612.name: Family Challenges
612.desc: An in-depth exploration of several family challenges (e.g., addiction and homelessness). An introduction to specific intervention approaches related to family challenges. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 412.
612.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

613.name: Graduate Practicum in Human Ecology
613.raw: Prerequisites: consent of Supervisor and Department.
613.desc: Selected practicum placements to integrate theory and practice in a variety of agencies. When used as the capping exercise for the course-based Master's program, requirements include a written report and an oral presentation to the Department and/or where appropriate to relevant agency staff.
613.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

615.name: Families and Aging
615.desc: Current issues in mid- and later-life families including relationships between aging parents and adult children, grandparent relationships, family caregiving. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 415.
615.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

617.name: Intimate Relationships
617.desc: In-depth examination of intimate relationships, including theoretical perspectives, research methods, relationship forms and processes, and how context affects relationships. Students will consider how sociological, psychological, and personal factors affect the development, maintenance and dissolution of intimate relationships today.
617.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

619.name: Work-Family Integration
619.desc: An examination of the complex relationship between two important social institutions: work and family. Topics include demographic, social, and economic changes that have shaped the work-family relationship as a contemporary issue; its implications for individuals, families, work environments and society; and theoretical and practical perspectives on the challenges of and strategies for managing the relationship.
619.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

640.name: Family Policy Issues
640.raw: Prerequisite: HECOL 300 or consent of instructor. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 440.
640.desc: An examination of the elements of policies and policy issues that affect contemporary Canadian families. The elements of policies and policy issues studied include: their origins and underlying ideologies; their institutional frameworks and foundations; and their substance, nature, and impact on families.
640.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

654.name: Research Project in Human Ecology
654.desc: An original research project, conducted with guidance from a faculty member, typically resulting in the preparation of a research report and a submission to a professional academic conference for a poster or paper presentation OR the preparation of a manuscript that is submitted to a scholarly journal for publication. May be taken more than once for credit.
654.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

661.name: Perspectives on Material Culture and Design Studies
661.desc: A critical analysis of specific issues, theories, and perspectives that influence material culture and design studies, as fields of research and practice. This course looks into designed things, from clothing to urban environments, and is focused on supporting students as they explore issues and develop theories connected to their research.
661.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

662.name: Themes in Material Culture and Sustainability
662.desc: An exploration of human engagements with material things (and/or places) through the consideration of aspects of their production, mediation, and/or consumption (including disposal). Topics are discussed through scholarship that is associated with (selected) disciplinary themes within the interdisciplinary and interconnected fields of material culture studies and sustainability studies.
662.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

664.name: Fashion and Material Culture: Politics, Economies, Societies, c. 1600-1900
664.raw: Prerequisite: consent of the instructor. Not to be taken if credit received for HECOL 464.
664.desc: Examines the evolution and practice of fashion as a social, economic, political and cultural phenomenon from a cross-cultural perspective.
664.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

668.name: Material Culture and Curatorship
668.desc: Examines the different ways in which artifacts-from the body to the built environment-are interpreted in physical and virtual exhibitions. The course is designed to include a variety of student interests but pieces from the Anne Lambert Clothing and Textiles Collection will serve as preferred artifacts for assignments. Guest lecturers and site visits add to lectures on museum practices such as handling and mounting, storage, registrarial processes, research and exhibition design. Students co-curate an exhibition as part of the course.
668.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

671.name: Topics in Family Science and Aging
671.desc: Topics of current interest in Family Science and Aging. May be taken for credit more than once.
671.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

672.name: Topics in Material Culture
672.desc: Topics of current interest in Material Culture studies. May be taken for credit more than once.
672.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

673.name: Topics in Textiles and Clothing
673.desc: Topics of current interest in Textiles and Clothing. May be taken for credit more than once.
673.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

682.name: Program Planning and Evaluation
682.desc: Theories, approaches, and processes fundamental to the development, implementation, and evaluation of programs that effect change and build capacity in families, communities and organizations.
682.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

691.name: Professional Seminar 1
691.desc: This professional development seminar is one in a series that provides an introduction to graduate study in the Department of Human Ecology, and to career development and professional issues in human ecology. Includes topics such as the field of human ecology, what it means to be a graduate student, and student-supervisor relationship. Typically taken in the first year of the graduate program.
691.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

692.name: Professional Seminar 2
692.desc: This professional development seminar is one in a series that focuses on career development and professional issues in human ecology. Includes topics such as writing for academic and non-academic audiences and research ethics. Typically taken in the first year of the graduate program.
692.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

693.name: Professional Seminar 3
693.desc: This professional development seminar is one in a series that focuses on career development and professional issues in human ecology. Includes topics such as the process of the doctoral program and comprehensive and candidacy exams. Typically taken in the second year of the doctoral program.
693.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

694.name: Professional Seminar 4
694.desc: This professional development seminar is one in a series that focuses on career development and professional issues in human ecology. Includes topics such as funding agencies and preparing grant proposals, non-academic careers for PhDs, and post-doctoral fellowships. Typically taken in the second year of the doctoral program.
694.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

900.name: Directed Research Project
900.desc: Comprises the capping exercise for the course-based Masters programs. Requirements include conducting an applied research project, and both a written project report and an oral presentation to the Department, and where appropriate, to relevant practising professionals.
900.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

613A.name: Graduate Practicum in Human Ecology
613A.raw: Prerequisites: consent of Supervisor and Department.
613A.desc: Selected practicum placements to integrate theory and practice in a variety of agencies. When used as the capping exercise for the course-based Master's program, requirements include a written report and an oral presentation to the Department and/or where appropriate to relevant agency staff.
613A.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

613B.raw: Prerequisites: consent of Supervisor and Department.
613B.desc: Selected practicum placements to integrate theory and practice in a variety of agencies. When used as the capping exercise for the course-based Master's program, requirements include a written report and an oral presentation to the Department and/or where appropriate to relevant agency staff.
613B.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

654A.desc: An original research project, conducted with guidance from a faculty member, typically resulting in the preparation of a research report and a submission to a professional academic conference for a poster or paper presentation OR the preparation of a manuscript that is submitted to a scholarly journal for publication. May be taken more than once for credit.
654A.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

900B.name: Directed Research Project
900B.desc: Comprises the capping exercise for the course-based Masters programs. Requirements include conducting an applied research project, and both a written project report and an oral presentation to the Department, and where appropriate, to relevant practising professionals.
900B.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

100.name: Introduction to Human Geography and Planning
100.desc: The spatial organization of human landscapes, and significance of the distribution of human activity. Not available to students with credit in HGP 100.

240.name: Cities and Urbanism
240.raw: Prerequisite: Any 3 unit course. Not available to students with credit in HGP 240.
240.desc: Introduction to urban geography and planning emphasizing interactions between the built environment and processes of social and economic change. Topics include urban form, housing and diversity in North American cities.

250.name: Sustainable Development and Environmental Management
250.raw: Prerequisite: Any 3 unit course. Not available for students with credit in HGP 250 or SUST 201.
250.desc: An introduction to sustainable development approaches to dealing with environmental issues.

252.name: Human Dimensions of Environmental Hazards
252.raw: Prerequisite: Any 3 unit course. Not available to students with credit in HGP 252.
252.desc: Interactions between environmental hazards, individuals and communities; risk reduction strategies by members of the public and management agencies.

341.name: Social and Cultural Geography
341.raw: Prerequisites: HGP 100 or HGEO 100, and HGEO 240 or HGP 240. Not available for students with credit in HGP 341.
341.desc: Connections between space, society and culture at multiple scales. Formation and significance of cultural landscapes, and shaping of social life by spatial arrangements.

342.name: The Spatial Economy
342.raw: Prerequisites: HGEO 100 or HGP 100 and any HGEO 2XX or PLAN 2XX course. Not available for students with credit in HGP 342.
342.desc: Introduction to the study of the location, distribution and spatial organization of economic activities on both the local and the international scale.

343.name: Geographies of Health and Health Care
343.desc: Geographic perspectives on health and health care, including social, behavioural, and institutional factors.

381.name: Topics In Human Geography
381.raw: Prerequisite: HGP 100 or HGEO 100. Topics vary; may be taken more than once for credit provided no topic is repeated.
381.desc: Theory and application of contemporary issues in human geography.

382.name: Topics in Regional Geography
382.desc: Selected regions are studied in a regional or topical format. Topics vary; may be taken more than once for credit provided no topic is repeated.

399.name: Research Methods in Human Geography
399.raw: Prerequisites: HGEO 100 or HGP 100 and any HGEO 2XX, PLAN 2XX, or HGP 2XX course. Not available for students with credit in HGP 399.
399.desc: Collection and analysis of data for social research in human geography. Research design and sampling procedures. Both qualitative and quantitative methods are explored. Fieldwork required.

443.name: Environment and Health
443.desc: An examination of relations between human health and environmental issues, particularly those related to the natural, built, and social environments.

450.name: Resource Management and Environmental Policy
450.raw: Prerequisites: HGEO 250 or HGP 250; and any 300-level course. Not available for students with credit in HGP 450.
450.desc: Roles of governmental and nongovernmental organizations, industry and private enterprise, and advocacy organizations in addressing issues of resource scarcity and environmental policy. Institutions, policies, governance, and strategies for resource and environmental management at the provincial/state, national, and international levels.

452.name: Human Dimensions of Environmental Change
452.raw: Prerequisite: Any 300-level EAS, HGP or HGEO course or Consent of Instructor. Not available for students with credit in HGP 452.
452.desc: Examination of the human dimensions of climate change. Topics include climate change politics, public perceptions and impacts, vulnerability and resilience, mitigation and adaptation.

470.name: Geographical Information Systems for Social Science
470.raw: Prerequisite: EAS 221. Not available for students with credit in HGP 470 or PLAN 470.
470.desc: The application of spatial analytic tools to social science topics. Assignments impart technical aspects through hands-on experience with commercial and in-house spatial analysis software.

481.name: Advanced Topics in Human Geography
481.raw: Prerequisites: HGEO 100 or HGP 100, and any one HGEO 2XX or HGP 2XX course. Topics vary; may be taken more than once for credit provided no topic is repeated.

104.name: The Atomic Age: The World After 1945
104.desc: Introduction to key economic, political, and societal changes at the global scale.

110.name: The Pre-Modern World
110.desc: World history from the end of the 6th century to the 15th century.

111.name: The Early Modern World
111.desc: World history from the 15th century through the 18th century.

112.name: The Modern World
112.desc: The world since the beginning of the 19th century. Not open to students with credit in HIST 120.

114.name: The History of the World in the Last 10 Years
114.desc: Global historical developments over the last 10 years with emphasis on the interaction of states and peoples.

115.name: Technology and History
115.desc: The role of technology in historical developments around the world.

116.name: Colonization in the Americas
116.desc: The history of colonization in the Americas, European-Indigenous encounters, and the transatlantic slave trade that linked Europe, Africa, and the Americas during the early modern era, emphasizing economic, political, social and cultural legacies.

123.name: Plague: Disease and Epidemics in History
123.desc: The causes, impacts, and experiences of disease in human history.

124.name: History of Sexuality in the Americas
124.desc: History of sexual behaviour, identities, and regulations in the Western Hemisphere from the colonial era through the twentieth century.

127.name: Drugs in Modern Global History
127.desc: The social, cultural, and political histories of criminalized drugs like opium, marijuana, amphetamines, and cocaine.

128.name: War, Revolution, and Society
128.desc: The causes, course, and consequences of major conflicts around the globe, including their wider social effects.

130.name: Democracy, War and Consumer Capitalism: The Making of Modern Europe
130.desc: European history from the Enlightenment to the present.

134.name: Global History of Alchemy: Quests for Gold, Power, and Immortality
134.desc: Theories and practices of ancient and medieval alchemy in its historical and cultural contexts.

135.name: Origins of Ancient India: Cities, Migrations and Peoples
135.desc: Introduction to the formative period of South Asian history, from approximately 3000 BCE to 600 CE, covering the Harappan civilization, Indo-European migration, and the first kingdoms of the Ganges valley.

179.name: Sex Work and Intimate Labour in Global History

191.name: Video Games, History, and Storytelling
191.desc: The use of world history in video games.

195.name: Warfare Since 1789: From Mass Armies to Thermonuclear War

203.name: History of Computing
203.desc: Survey of the history of computers, computing, and human/computer interactions.

205.name: Capitalism
205.desc: The development of global capitalism through an exploration of historical changes in trade, markets, ideas, work, consumption, and government policies.

207.name: From Constantine to the Cathedral: Europe in the Middle Ages
207.desc: A survey of Europe from the fourth to the thirteenth century.

212.name: Early Modern Europe
212.desc: A survey of European history from approximately 1200 to 1800.

219.name: Famine as Genocide in the 20th Century: The Case of the Holodomor
219.desc: Exploration of the 1932-33 famine in Ukraine in the context of other 20th century famines, genocide, survivor experience, and Soviet history.

220.name: The Making of the Modern Middle East
220.desc: Twentieth-century political and cultural history, following the Ottoman Empire's disintegration

237.name: The Pacific World Since 1500
237.desc: Exploration, migration, trade, and geopolitics in the Pacific region, connecting Australia and the Pacific Islands with Asia and coastal North and South America.

241.name: Colonial Latin America
241.desc: Survey of Latin American history to 1810.

242.name: Modern Latin America
242.desc: Survey of Latin American history since 1810.

243.name: The Golden Age of Islam: History of the Muslim World to the 16th Century
243.desc: Historical overview of the rise of Islam in seventh century Arabia and the political, economic and cultural impact of subsequent expansion into Asia, Africa and Europe.

246.name: Africa from Medieval to Modern Times

247.name: Africa in the 20th and 21st Centuries: From Colonial Rule to Modern Nations

250.name: American History to 1865
250.desc: Survey of United States history from colonial times to the Civil War.

251.name: From the End of Slavery to the Present: American History Since 1865
251.desc: Survey of United States history from the Civil War to the present.

252.name: Slavery in the Americas
252.desc: Comparative examination of slavery in the Western Hemisphere from its creation to abolition.

272.name: Religion in History
272.desc: A study of a religious tradition(s), its teachings and rituals, along with its function in a specific historical setting, including its role in conditioning and reflecting a particular society and culture.

280.name: East Asia to 1500
280.desc: Survey of history of East Asia (China, Korea, Japan, Vietnam) to 1500.

281.name: East Asia from 1500
281.desc: Survey of the history of East Asia (China, Korea, Japan, Vietnam) from 1500 to the present.

285.name: China and the West
285.desc: A survey of Chinese-Western cultural interactions from the time of Marco Polo to the present.

289.name: Classical India to 500 CE
289.desc: The world of Classical India, from the emergence of the Mauryan Empire in the fourth century BCE to the close of the Gupta Empire in the fifth century CE.

290.name: Introduction to History as a Discipline
290.raw: Prerequisite: A previous course in History or consent of the Department.
290.desc: Introduction to the basic concepts of historical inquiry and techniques of research and writing in History. Course includes lectures and discussions. Required for History majors.

291.name: World War One
291.desc: The European conflict and its global dimensions, with an emphasis on political, social, and cultural histories.

292.name: Medieval India from 500 to 1500 CE
292.desc: A survey of the history of India from the close of the Gupta and Vakataka kingdoms in the fifth century CE to the decline of the Delhi Sultanate and the Vijayanagara Empire in the sixteenth century CE.

293.name: History of Science, Technology and Medicine: Key Moments
293.desc: Pivotal events in the history of science, technology, and medicine using a wide variety of historical sources, such as photographs, artifacts, films, letters, and diaries.

294.name: An Introduction to the History of Sciences, Technology, and Medicine
294.desc: Broad survey of topics in the history of science, technology, and medicine.

295.name: 20th-Century Warfare
295.desc: In-depth look at some of the conflicts of the 20th century, the course examines wars and revolutions including the two world wars, the Korean and Vietnam wars, African guerrilla wars, and the Gulf War. Analyze the causes and consequences of war and the evolution of weaponry. To be offered in alternate years.

296.name: World War Two
296.desc: The global conflict, with emphasis on political, social, scientific, and cultural aspects.

297.name: The History of Christianity
297.desc: Lecture and discussion course about the development of Christian traditions in the world.

298.name: State and Society in Mughal India
298.desc: A political and social history of India from the 16th-19th centuries, focusing on the Mughal empire.

299.name: Gandhi, Resistance, and Non-violence
299.desc: Introduction to the history and legacy of Mahatma Gandhi. Topics may include Gandhi's influence on India's national freedom movement from colonial rule, his application of non-violence as a method of resistance, and the ways in which his religious worldview shaped his ideology and actions.

301.name: Europe in the Age of Total War, 1890-1945
301.desc: European experience with total war, economic crisis, cultural change and totalitarian regimes in the new era of mass politics and Great Power conflict.

302.name: Germany in the 20th Century and Beyond
302.desc: The economic, social, cultural, and political histories of the various Germanies in their European and global contexts, from 1900 to the present.

303.name: Saints and Medieval Christianity
303.desc: Beginning with the early Christian background, this course treats the various forms of sanctity (martyrs, monks and clerics) that appeared in medieval Europe, along with the social functions that the cult of the saints fulfilled in the world of Late Antiquity and the Middle Ages.

308.name: Sexuality and Gender in Modern Europe
308.desc: Introduction to the social organization, cultural construction, and political dimensions of sexuality and gender in Europe from the eighteenth to the twenty-first centuries.

309.name: The History of Paris
309.desc: Introduction to the history of Paris from late antiquity to the present day, drawing on film, music, art, philosophy, geography, architecture, and literature.

310.name: A History of the Habsburg Monarchy, 1526-1918
310.desc: The multinational empire of the Habsburgs from the unification of Austria, Bohemia and Hungary to the destruction of the empire in World War I.

311.name: History of Vienna
311.desc: Introduction to the history of Vienna from prehistoric times to the present day, drawing on film, music, art, geography, architecture, and literature.

312.name: Foundations of East European History
312.desc: The ethnic, religious, social, and political factors which shaped the development of the peoples of Eastern Europe from the Middle Ages through the Age of Enlightenment. Intended as background to the later histories of the Balkans, 'Central Europe', and Ukraine.

313.name: Medieval and Early Imperial Russia
313.desc: Russia from Kievan Rus' through Catherine the Great's reign, 900s to 1800. Note: Not open to students with credit in HIST 318.

315.name: Topics in Global History
315.desc: Addresses historical processes or themes affecting diverse areas of the world. Can be repeated if course content varies.

318.name: Modern Ukraine
318.desc: Ukrainian history from the late eighteenth century to the present. Note: Not open to students with credit in HIST 315, 316, or 317.

320.name: Russia from Reform to Revolution, 1800-1917
320.desc: Reaction, reform, and revolution, from Paul I to Nicholas II. Note: Not open to students with credit in HIST 318.

322.name: Russia in the 20th Century
322.desc: An historical survey of domestic and foreign policy, from Nicholas II to Yeltsin.

323.name: The Middle East in the Making: 1300-1920
323.desc: The rise and demise of the Ottoman Empire. An overview of the religious, cultural and political making of current-day North Africa, Near and Middle East, and Eastern Mediterranean. HIST 111 and 112 are recommended but not required.

326.name: Topics in History at the Movies
326.desc: Provides students with the historical tools to analyze history as it is presented in movies. Topics will vary according to the instructor(s).

338.name: Topics in Indigenous History
338.desc: Addresses select themes in the histories of Indigenous peoples. Can be repeated if course content varies.

339.name: The Modern British Empire and the Commonwealth Experience

344.name: Global Environmental History
344.desc: Histories of interactions between non-human nature and diverse cultures, with attention to inequality and environmental change.

350.name: Slavery and Abolition in Africa
350.desc: Explores slave trading out of Africa, domestic slavery within it, and European policies that were used to justify conquering and colonizing the continent. Course materials may include primary documents and images, slave narratives, historical fiction, and videos.

351.name: History of Women in the United States
351.desc: A multicultural and multiracial history of women from the colonial period to the present.

352.name: African American History from Slavery to Black Power
352.desc: The African American experience in the United States from the colonial era to the present.

353.name: History of American Medicine
353.desc: The social history of American health care and health practitioners. How sickness, health, and healing have changed over the course of American history.

359.name: Canadian Environmental History
359.desc: Brings the natural environment onto a shared stage with social, economic, political and cultural history in Canada from the last ice age to the present.

362.name: History of Alberta
362.desc: Economic, social, and political realities that underlie the many images of Alberta.

365.name: The Canadian West to 1885
365.desc: Native diplomacy and warfare, the development of fur trade societies, and European colonization to the suppression of the North-West Rebellion.

366.name: The Canadian West Since 1885
366.desc: Economic, social, and political aspects of regional alienation, identity, and protest.

368.name: Histories of Indigenous Peoples and Kanata until 1870
368.desc: Examines selected themes of the histories of Indigenous Peoples in what is now known as Canada (or Kanata, a word in Iroquoian meaning village or settlement) from Time Immemorial until 1870.

369.name: Histories of Indigenous Peoples and Kanata after 1870
369.desc: Examines selected themes of the histories of Indigenous Peoples in what is now known as Canada (or Kanata, a word in Iroquoian meaning village or settlement) after 1870.

370.name: Making War in Canada
370.desc: History of war and conflict within Canada.

373.name: Peasants, Slaves and Workers
373.desc: The history of work regimes and regulation from feudalism to the present.

377.name: Canada Since 1945
377.desc: Economic, political, social and cultural developments in the postwar era.

378.name: Topics in the History of the United States

379.name: Religion in Modern Europe
379.desc: Religious revival and secularization in Europe from the French Revolution to the present. Topics include: relations between church and state; intellectual challenges and responses; and religion transformed by modernity.

383.name: The Civilization and Culture of Early China
383.desc: This course focuses on the formative periods of Chinese civilization from prehistory to circa 600.

384.name: History of Chinese Philosophy
384.desc: Historical development of the major philosophical traditions in pre-modern China.

385.name: Modern China
385.raw: Prerequisites: 3 units from EASIA 101, HIST 280, 281, 285 or 290, or consent of Department.
385.desc: The history of China from the late nineteenth century to the present.

386.name: History of Science in Ancient and Classical India
386.desc: Indigenous scientific activities and achievements of ancient and classical India, from 500 BCE to 1400 CE.

387.name: History of Indian Yoga and Meditation
387.desc: The history and philosophy of early Yoga, exploring its focus on meditation, its literature, its connections with Buddhism, and its historical evolution. HIST 110, 289, or CLASS 110 are recommended but not required.

390.name: Imperial China from circa 600 to 1911
390.desc: The institutional and social history of imperial China from the Tang to the Manchu Ch'ing dynasties.

392.name: Ancient India- Diversity in History
392.desc: Taking the case of ancient India, this course highlights how diversity can be explained in a multicultural society and how it defines the character of civilization on the sub-continent.

394.name: History of Astronomy and Cosmology from Stonehenge to the Space Age
394.desc: An examination of the major themes in the history of astronomy and cosmology from the ancient world to the present day.
