101.desc: Topics relevant to successful academic performance including study skills, use of campus resources, stress management, and career planning.
101.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

102.name: First-Year Experience II
102.desc: Exploration and application of university regulations, faculty expectations, pathways to academic excellence, and practical methods for surviving the challenges of first year on campus.
102.faculty: Faculty of Agricultural, Life and Environmental Sciences

499.name: Undergraduate Research
499.desc: Represents research activity for registration status. This course cannot be used towards a degree program.

101.name: Representations of Girls and Women
101.desc: An exploration of the impact that cultural representations of gender have on the political, economic, and social lives of girls and women throughout the world.

102.name: Gender and Social Justice
102.desc: Examines social and cultural constructions of gender, sexuality, race, class, and disability as well as visions for social justice.

220.name: Feminism and Popular Culture
220.desc: Selected cultural forms from feminist perspectives. The focus is both on developing a feminist critique of cultural representations of women, and on considering the possibilities of feminist intervention in and production of popular culture.

230.name: Consent
230.desc: An interdisciplinary exploration of the concept of sexual consent. Topics covered may include: the role of sexual violence in colonization, feminist law reform, unwanted sex, sexual  agency, sexual fraud, and the limitations of consent- based prevention.

240.name: Feminism and Food
240.desc: Introduction to food justice and feminist food politics.

244.name: Critical Disability Studies
244.desc: Introduction to social and cultural models of disability, with an emphasis on intersections of disability with race, class, gender, and sexuality.

250.name: Gender and Science
250.desc: Interdisciplinary exploration of gender and science, with an emphasis on intersections of gender, race, sexuality, and politics in historical and contemporary scientific practices.

255.name: Gender and Sexuality in World and Indigenous Religions
255.desc: Historical and contemporary survey of ideas about, and practices relating to, gender and sexuality in world and Indigenous religions.

260.name: Women and War
260.desc: Introduction to how women experience political conflicts, either in contemporary or historical contexts, focusing on how violence, access to resources, public decision-making, and social security impact women during and after conflict.

270.name: Feminism and Sexualities
270.desc: Approaches to, and key debates about, sexuality. Topics may include: sexology; critiques of heterosexuality; political lesbianism; queer theory; transgender and intersexuality; prostitution and sex work.

280.name: Indigenous Women, Autobiography, and Life Writing
280.desc: Explores the ways in which Indigenous women have resisted colonial constructions of race and gender through autobiographical expressions and life writing. Includes study of memoirs, journals, confessions, diaries, personal essays, oral histories, and visual art.

290.name: Feminism and Animals
290.desc: Feminist contributions to animal ethics, critical animal studies, and animal-focused work in feminist environmental humanities and social sciences.

298.name: Critical Issues
298.desc: This course offers an introduction to select issues in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies. A variable content course, which may be repeated if topics vary.

301.name: History of Feminist Thought
301.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
301.desc: Historical study of selected feminist writers and activists. Emphasis is on European and North American feminist thought up to the mid twentieth century.

302.name: Feminist Research and Methodologies
302.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or departmental consent.
302.desc: Exploration of feminist modes of research inquiry, feminist ethics in research, and critiques of traditional disciplinary approaches to research. Students will develop an understanding of theoretical issues involved in feminist research and will gain practical research skills.

310.name: Gender and Social Justice in Contemporary Africa
310.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
310.desc: The lives of men and women in contemporary Africa, focusing on their experiences in the family, school, paid work, and the market, and on such development issues as health, environment, and human rights.

315.name: Histories of Gender
315.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
315.desc: Introduction to a range of practices and ideas concerning women, gender, and kinship that characterized societies and cultures around the globe before the twentieth century.

321.name: Feminism and Film
321.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
321.desc: Feminist analysis of gender, sexuality, ability, race/ethnicity, and class/status in film. Content will vary in terms of genre, production, and language.

332.name: Contemporary Feminist Theory
332.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
332.desc: The origins and evolution of various schools of contemporary western feminist thought.

360.name: Race, Class, and Gender
360.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
360.desc: Historical, contemporary and comparative perspectives on the interaction of race, class, and gender experiences.

365.name: Gender, Conflict and Peace Building
365.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS or W ST course, or consent of Department.
365.desc: The analysis of gender in international relations, drawing from literature on conflict and post conflict relations.

370.name: Queer Theory
370.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or departmental consent.
370.desc: A survey of core texts and key debates that have shaped queer theory.

380.name: Canadian Feminist Activisms
380.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
380.desc: An examination of contemporary feminist activisms with an emphasis on second- and third-wave feminisms. This course may be offered as a Community Service Learning course.

390.name: Environmental Feminisms and Social Justice
390.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
390.desc: Addresses issues of environmental racism, sexism, and ableism, feminist approaches to environmental ethics, and social justice responses to climate change.

401.name: Directed Readings in Women's and Gender Studies
401.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
401.desc: Open only to Women's and Gender Studies honors, majors and minors. Normally may be taken only once.

404.name: Trans & Queer Game Design
404.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department., or consent of department.
404.desc: Through a combination of playing, reading, and collaborative making, students in this course will dive into the world of trans and queer interactive media art. Students will engage experimental works from emerging game artists and will explore how these designers make space for trans and queer play in their work. Credit will only be granted once for MST 404 or WGS 404. Through a combination of playing, reading, and collaborative making, students in this course will dive into the world of trans and queer interactive media art. Students will engage experimental works from emerging game artists and will explore how these designers make space for trans and queer play in their work. Credit will only be granted once for MST 404 or WGS 404.

420.name: Law and Feminism in Canada
420.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or departmental consent.
420.desc: A focus on the fundamentally contradictory role of law for women in Canada, building upon role of insights offered by feminist cross-disciplinary legal scholarship.

431.name: Feminism and Sexual Assault
431.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or departmental consent.
431.desc: Interdisciplinary consideration of conceptual, political and legal strategies that feminists have deployed to confront sexual coercion with an emphasis on contemporary North American context.

440.name: Body Politics
440.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
440.desc: An examination of contemporary theoretical approaches to bodies and embodiment, with particular emphasis on the ways that race, class, sexuality, gender, and (dis)ability shape bodily experience.

450.name: Transnational Feminism
450.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS or consent of department.
450.desc: This course engages in women's issues globally and across nations. Topics may include feminist theorizing, women's movements, development, human rights, reproductive politics and social governance.

455.name: Religion, Spirituality, and Social Justice
455.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
455.desc: Ways in which adherents of world (Eastern and Western), Indigenous, and neo-pagan religious systems have advocated for social justice.

460.name: Masculinities
460.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
460.desc: This course surveys the status of masculinity and the emergence of contemporary masculinity studies.

470.name: Sexualities: Special Topics
470.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
470.desc: This course offers advanced examination of selected issues in sexuality studies.

475.name: Indigenous Genders and Sexualities
475.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or departmental consent.
475.desc: Exploration of gender diversity and sexualities from Indigenous and Indigenous feminist worldviews, including critical examination of colonial constructions of gender and sexuality.

480.name: Indigenous Feminisms
480.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or consent of department.
480.desc: Draws on Indigenous theoretical frameworks, epistemologies, community expertise and knowledge to understand Indigenous women's participation in political movements and land and environmental activism. Students are strongly urged to complete 3 units in NS before registering in WGS 480.

498.name: Special Topics
498.raw: Prerequisite: Any 100 or 200 level WGS course, or departmental consent.

100.name: Topics in Academic Writing
100.desc: An introduction to the theory and practice of writing in various disciplines.

101.name: Exploring Writing
101.desc: This workshop course focuses on both the theory and practice of the writing process to help students experience firsthand how university writers enter into rich ongoing conversations by engaging with the words and ideas of others.

102.name: Writing in the Disciplines
102.desc: Introduces students to academic writing in three broad areas: humanities, social sciences, and sciences. May be offered in a blended (combining online work and in-person meetings), online, or another format. No prerequisite. May not be repeated.

103.name: An Introduction to Writing in the Sciences
103.desc: Basic principles and genres of writing for science students. Note: Restricted to students in the Faculty of Science.

104.name: Writing Persuasive Arguments
104.desc: Introduction to the principles, theories and practice of writing well supported and convincing arguments.

201.name: Peer Tutor Training in Writing
prereqs: WRS 3 units WRS at the 100 level
201.raw: Prerequisites: 3 units WRS at the 100 level.
201.desc: Introduction to practices and strategies for tutoring undergraduate writers focusing on online and ESL writers.

203.name: Writing in the Sciences
203.raw: Prerequisites: 3 in 100-level ENGL or 100-level WRS, or consent of instructor. Note: credit will not begranted for both WRS 103 and WRS 203.
203.desc: An introduction to writing in the sciences as a practice through which core values of scientific research are communicated and sustained. Students analyze and produce research-based multimodal scientific genres for both academic and public audiences

206.name: Writing Special Effects: Rhetorical Grammar and Style
206.raw: Prerequisites: 3 units selected from 100-level ENGL or 100-level WRS (or consent of instructor).
206.desc: Analysis of and practice in sentence structures to create/alter meaning and voice in nonfiction prose.

210.name: Introduction to Professional Communication
210.desc: Analysis of and practice in key genres, processes, and strategies for professional communication.

301.name: Introduction to Writing Centre Practice
301.raw: Prerequisites: 6 units selected from 100-level ENGL or 100-level WRS (or consent of instructor).
301.desc: Introduces students to the primary themes of interdisciplinary writing studies and collaborative learning necessary to successfully work as peer writing coaches in a university writing centre. Building on the foundation of theory, the course guides students through coaching sessions to synthesize an appropriate coaching practice.

305.name: Risk Communication
305.raw: Prerequisites: 6 units selected from 100-level ENGL or 100-level WRS or consent of the instructor.
305.desc: Basic principles and processes of written forms of risk communication within the context of theoretical issues of the public's right to know, rhetorical effectiveness, cultural awareness, and ethics.

311.name: Editing Texts
311.raw: Prerequisites: 6 units selected from 100-level ENGL or 100-level WRS (or consent of instructor).
311.desc: Students will learn the skills required to transform manuscripts into publishable form for print and digital platforms.

450.name: Capstone Portfolio Project
450.raw: Prerequisites: 12 units selected from WRS, or consent of instructor.
450.desc: Revision of documents and writing of new documents to create a portfolio of writing.

603.name: Writing Centre Theory
603.desc: Introducing students to research in writing studies with a focus on writing in the disciplines and in writing centres.

101A.name: Exploring Writing
101A.desc: This workshop course focuses on both the theory and practice of the writing process to help students experience firsthand how university writers enter into rich ongoing conversations by engaging with the words and ideas of others.

101B.desc: This workshop course focuses on both the theory and practice of the writing process to help students experience firsthand how university writers enter into rich ongoing conversations by engaging with the words and ideas of others.

224.name: Vertebrate Diversity
224.desc: A comparative survey of vertebrates, focusing on their morphology, classification, and phylogeny.

241.name: Animal Physiology I: Homeostasis
241.raw: Prerequisite: BIOL 107. This course may not be taken for credit if credit has been obtained in PHYSL 210 or PHYSL 212.
241.desc: Survey of physiological systems that regulate levels of gases, food, energy, temperature, water, and ions. Examples from invertebrates and vertebrates.

242.name: Animal Physiology II: Intercellular Communication
242.raw: Prerequisite: BIOL 107. This course may not be taken for credit if credit has been obtained in PHYSL 210 or PHYSL 214.
242.desc: Endocrinology, immunology and neural, sensory, motor, and reproductive physiology. Examples from invertebrates and vertebrates.

250.name: Survey of the Invertebrates
250.desc: The functional anatomy and life cycles of the major invertebrate taxa are emphasized.

303.name: Animal Developmental Biology
303.raw: Prerequisite: BIOL 201 or CELL 201.
303.desc: An introduction to basic principles in animal development both in vertebrates and invertebrates. This course examines how the molecular, cellular and comparative approaches are integrated to explain the development of the egg into the embryo, and the cellular interactions that culminate in the development of organ systems.

325.name: Comparative Anatomy of the Vertebrates
325.raw: Prerequisite: a 200-level ZOOL course; ZOOL 224 strongly recommended. May not be taken for credit if credit already obtained in ZOOL 225.
325.desc: A comparative survey of form and function in vertebrate animals. Lectures focus on patterns of evolution and adaptation. Laboratories offer detailed examinations of major organ systems in representative species.

340.name: Comparative Environmental Physiology
340.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 241 or  PHYSL 210 or 212 or 214.
340.desc: A comparative examination of the integrated responses of animals to environmental changes. This course focuses on both the acute physiological and long-term adaptations to dealing with environmental challenges. Focus is on biochemical and physiological responses to extreme environments.

342.name: Neurobiology
342.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 242 or PHYSL 210 or 212. Students who have taken PMCOL 371 may not receive credit in ZOOL 342.
342.desc: Nerve cells, nervous systems and neuromuscular systems from molecular, physiological, behavioral, and developmental perspectives. Examples from both invertebrates and vertebrates are given.

343.name: Comparative Endocrinology
343.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 242 or PHYSL 210 or 212 or 214.
343.desc: Endocrine systems and actions of hormones at the tissue, cell and molecular levels; vertebrate systems are emphasized.

344.name: Laboratory Exercises in Animal Physiology
344.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 241 or  242 or PHYSL 210 or 212 or 214.
344.desc: Physiological topics are reinforced in experimental lab exercises. Labs include computer simulations, artificial tissue models and animal models.

350.name: Biology and Evolution of Invertebrates
350.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 250. ZOOL 303 and ZOOL 351 recommended. Credit can only be obtained for one of ZOOL 350, 450 or 550. Offered in alternate years.
350.desc: Invertebrate evolution and adaptations including topics on feeding and nutrition, motility, reproduction and development, and sensory systems. Emphasis will be on material from the primary literature. Laboratory exercises will involve advanced training in techniques of microscopy.

351.name: Freshwater Invertebrate Diversity
351.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 250. Offered in alternate years.
351.desc: Emphasis is on an identified collection of invertebrates found in Alberta's lakes and streams. Lecture material pertains mainly to ecological features of the various fresh water groups.

352.name: Principles of Parasitism
352.raw: Prerequisite: a 200-level Biological Sciences course (ZOOL 250 or IMIN 200 recommended).
352.desc: An introduction to protozoan, helminth and arthropod parasites of animals; principles of host and parasite adaptation, epidemiology, ecology, host defenses and immunology, and control of parasitic infections. The seminar will highlight the diversity of parasites in the major groups.

370.name: Ethological Mechanisms
370.raw: Prerequisite or corequisite: ZOOL 241 or 242 or PHYSL 210, or 212 or 214.
370.desc: Animal behavior from an ethological perspective, with emphasis on the mechanisms underlying a variety of behaviors. The material is intended to complement that of ZOOL 371.

371.name: Behavioral Ecology
371.desc: Animal behavior from an ecological and evolutionary perspective, with emphasis on social behavior. The material is intended to complement that of ZOOL 370.  Prerequisite: BIOL 208

402.name: Current Topics in Developmental Biology
402.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 303 and consent of instructor. Credit for this course may be obtained more than once. Offered in alternate years.
402.desc: Discussion of selected topics in animal developmental biology from a molecular and cellular perspective. Evaluation of the primary literature and communication skills are emphasized.

405.name: Biology of Fishes
405.raw: Prerequisites: ZOOL 325 or both ZOOL 224 and a 300-level Biological Sciences course. Offered in alternate years.
405.desc: A survey of fish diversity focussing on the morphology, systematics, behavior, and ecology of the major groups. Laboratories feature extensive use of departmental collections, with an emphasis on Alberta species.

406.name: Biology of Amphibians and Reptiles
406.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 325 or both ZOOL 224 and a 300-level Biological Sciences course. Offered in alternate years.
406.desc: A survey of amphibian and reptile diversity focussing on morphology, systematics, behaviour, and ecology of major groups, within a phylogenetic and evolutionary framework. Laboratories feature extensive use of departmental collections, and include Albertan species. This course will normally include traditional lectures and student seminars.

407.name: Biology of Birds
407.raw: Prerequisites: ZOOL 325 or both ZOOL 224 and a 300-level Biological Sciences course.
407.desc: A survey of bird diversity focussing on the morphology, systematics, behaviour, and ecology of the major groups. Laboratories feature extensive use of departmental collections, with an emphasis on Alberta species.

408.name: Biology of Mammals
408.raw: Prerequisites: ZOOL 325 or both ZOOL 224 and a 300-level Biological Sciences course.
408.desc: A survey of mammal diversity focussing on the morphology, systematics, behavior, and ecology of the major groups. Laboratories feature extensive use of departmental collections, with an emphasis on Alberta species.

441.name: Current Topics on Homeostasis
441.raw: Prerequisites: ZOOL 340 or 342 or 343, or PHYSL 372, and consent of instructor. Credit for this course may be obtained more than once. Offered in alternate years.
441.desc: Discussion of selected topics in cardiac, gut, renal, respiratory, temperature, and metabolic physiology. Evaluation of the primary literature and communication skills are emphasized.

442.name: Current Topics in Intercellular Communication
442.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 342 or 343 or 352 or PMCOL 371 and consent of Department. Credit for this course may be obtained more than once. Offered in alternate years.
442.desc: Discussion of selected topics in endocrinology, immunology, and neurobiology from molecular, cellular, and whole-animal perspectives. Evaluation of the primary literature and communication skills are emphasized.

452.name: Topics in Parasitology
452.raw: Prerequisite: ZOOL 352 or MMI 426 or consent of Department. Credit cannot be obtained for both ZOOL 452 and ZOOL 552.
452.desc: This course covers topics of parasitology with emphasis on parasite diversity, evolutionary biology of parasitism, eco-immunology and biodiversity, and the future of parasitology. Specific vertebrate host immunity strategies against protozoan and helminth parasites, vector immunity, parasite evasion strategies, and pathology and disease associated with parasitic infections will also be covered. Lectures will be followed by active discussions of selected readings pertaining to current research in the subject area.

502.name: Advanced Current Topics in Developmental Biology
502.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor. Credit may be obtained more than once. Offered in alternate years.
502.desc: Discussion of selected topics in animal developmental biology from a molecular and cellular perspective. Evaluation of the primary literature and communication skills are emphasized. Discussions are the same as for ZOOL 402, but with additional assignments and evaluation appropriate to graduate studies.

541.name: Advanced Current Topics on Homeostasis
541.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor. Credit may be obtained more than once. Offered in alternate years.
541.desc: Discussion of selected topics in cardiac, gut, renal, respiratory, temperature, and metabolic physiology. Evaluation of the primary literature and communication skills are emphasized. Discussions are the same as for ZOOL 441, but with additional assignments and evaluation appropriate to graduate studies.

542.name: Advanced Current Topics in Intercellular Communication
542.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor. Credit may be obtained more than once. Offered in alternate years.
542.desc: Discussion of selected topics in endocrinology, immunology, and neurobiology from molecular, cellular, and whole-animal perspectives. Evaluation of the primary literature and communication skills are emphasized. Discussions are the same as for ZOOL 442, but with additional assignments and evaluation appropriate to graduate studies.

550.name: Advanced Biology and Evolution of Invertebrates
550.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor. Credit can only be obtained for one of ZOOL 350, 450 or 550. Offered in alternate years.
550.desc: Invertebrate evolution and adaptations including topics on feeding and nutrition, motility, reproduction and development, and sensory systems. Emphasis will be on material from the primary literature. Laboratory exercises will involve advanced training in techniques of microscopy. Lectures and labs are the same as for ZOOL 350, but with additional assignments and evaluation appropriate to graduate studies.

552.name: Advanced Topics in Parasitology
552.raw: Prerequisite: consent of instructor. Credit cannot be obtained for both ZOOL 452 and 552.
552.desc: Experimental approaches to the study of parasitism, including topics on epidemiology, ecology, biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, molecular biology, pathology, and immunology of host-parasite relationships. Reading assignments emphasize experimental approaches to study eukaryotic host-parasite relationships. Lectures are the same as for ZOOL 452, but with additional assignments and evaluation appropriate to graduate studies.

352.name: Principes du parasitisme
352.desc: Une introduction des parasites protozoaires, helminthes et arthropodes affectant les animaux; principes d'adaptations hôtes-parasites, d'épidémiologie, d'écologie, de défenses des hôtes et immunologie et contrôle des infections parasitaires. Les séminaires mettront en évidence la diversité des parasites dans les groupes importants. Préalable(s): un cours de niveau 200 en biologie (ZOOL 250 ou IMIN ou IMINE 200 recommandés). Note: Ce cours n'est pas accessible aux étudiants ayant ou postulant des crédits pour ZOOL 352.
